item.content:encoded:
The AIxBio Fellowship 2027 is offering an intensive, fully funded opportunity for researchers, engineers, policy professionals, entrepreneurs and technically minded individuals interested in tackling important challenges at the intersection of advanced artificial intelligence and biosecurity.

Organised by ERA in partnership with the Cambridge Biosecurity Hub, the 10-week, full-time programme will take place in Cambridge, United Kingdom, from 18 January to 26 March 2027.

The fellowship is designed for people who want to work on some of the most important emerging challenges associated with increasingly capable AI and biological risks, including the potential for AI to amplify biological threats and global catastrophic biological risks.

Importantly, applicants do not need prior formal research experience to apply. The programme welcomes individuals from a wide range of backgrounds, including artificial intelligence, machine learning, software engineering, biology, policy, governance, security and entrepreneurship.

Successful fellows will receive a £10,000 total stipend, together with expert mentorship, research management, workshops, networking opportunities and operational support throughout the programme.

About the AIxBio Fellowship 2027

The AIxBio Fellowship is a specialised programme focused on the rapidly developing relationship between artificial intelligence and biosecurity.

As AI systems become increasingly capable, they may create both opportunities and risks in biological research and security. The fellowship aims to bring talented people from different technical and professional backgrounds together to work on problems that could help reduce serious biological risks.

The programme is particularly concerned with global catastrophic biological risks (GCBRs), including risks associated with engineered pandemics and biological threats that could potentially be amplified by advanced AI.

Rather than being limited to one academic discipline, the fellowship is deliberately interdisciplinary.

It can accommodate projects and work involving:

  • Artificial intelligence
  • Machine learning
  • AI safety
  • Biological AI
  • Biosecurity
  • Biological risk reduction
  • Biosecurity safeguards
  • Policy
  • Governance
  • Security
  • Technology implementation
  • Research
  • Entrepreneurship
  • Other related areas at the AI-biosecurity intersection

This interdisciplinary approach means that the programme can be relevant to people who approach biosecurity from technical, scientific, policy, governance, security or entrepreneurial perspectives.

Who Is the AIxBio Fellowship Designed For?

The programme welcomes a broad range of applicants who are interested in addressing important problems involving AI and biosecurity.

Potential applicants include:

  • Graduate students
  • Early-career researchers
  • Experienced researchers
  • AI and machine-learning professionals
  • Software engineers
  • Biologists
  • Policy researchers
  • Governance professionals
  • Security professionals
  • Entrepreneurs and founders
  • Technically minded generalists
  • Professionals working on AI safety
  • Individuals interested in biological security
  • Professionals working at the intersection of technology and public policy

The programme is particularly interested in people who can bring useful expertise, technical skills, research abilities, policy knowledge or entrepreneurial thinking to important AI-biosecurity problems.

No Prior Formal Research Experience Required

One of the notable features of the AIxBio Fellowship is that prior formal research experience is not required.

This makes the programme potentially accessible to people who have strong technical, professional or interdisciplinary backgrounds but have not yet established a traditional academic research career.

While previous research experience can be useful, applicants are not required to have an extensive publication record or formal research background.

Instead, applicants can demonstrate their potential through their:

  • Technical abilities
  • Problem-solving skills
  • Professional experience
  • Research interests
  • Policy experience
  • Entrepreneurial experience
  • Understanding of AI or biology
  • Interest in biosecurity
  • Ability to work on complex interdisciplinary problems
  • Motivation to address global catastrophic biological risks

What Is the Main Focus of the Fellowship?

The central focus of the programme is the intersection between advanced AI and biosecurity.

This includes exploring how AI could influence biological risks and how technology, research, policy and governance can be used to reduce those risks.

The fellowship particularly focuses on reducing global catastrophic biological risks, including potential risks associated with engineered pandemics and biological threats that could be amplified by increasingly capable AI systems.

The programme therefore provides an opportunity for fellows to examine questions around how advanced technologies should be developed, governed and deployed in ways that reduce catastrophic risks.

Fellowship Tracks

The AIxBio Fellowship offers three primary tracks:

  1. Research
  2. Placement
  3. Founding

These tracks provide different ways for fellows to contribute to the programme depending on their background, interests and career objectives.

Research Track

The Research Track is suitable for participants who want to investigate important questions related to AI and biosecurity.

Research projects may address topics across areas such as:

  • AI safety
  • Biological AI
  • Biosecurity
  • AI-enabled biological risks
  • Risk assessment
  • Biosecurity safeguards
  • AI governance
  • Biological security
  • Technology policy
  • Global catastrophic biological risks

Participants can use the fellowship period to develop and investigate important questions while receiving support and mentorship.

The research environment can also provide an opportunity to develop ideas that may lead to future research projects, publications, policy work or other professional activities.

Placement Track

The Placement Track is designed to provide fellows with practical exposure and opportunities to work on relevant problems in an organisational or professional setting.

This track may be particularly attractive to individuals who want to apply their existing technical, research, policy or professional skills to real-world AI-biosecurity challenges.

A placement can help participants understand how organisations approach emerging technological and biological risks and how interdisciplinary expertise can be translated into practical solutions.

Founding Track

The Founding Track is designed for entrepreneurs and individuals interested in building organisations, initiatives or solutions addressing AI-biosecurity problems.

This track can be particularly relevant to founders and technically minded individuals who see opportunities to develop new tools, organisations or approaches to reducing biological risks associated with advanced AI.

The programme’s support can help participants develop their ideas, strengthen their understanding of the problem space and connect with relevant experts and networks.

What Does the Fellowship Provide?

The AIxBio Fellowship offers a combination of financial support, professional development, expert guidance and networking.

£10,000 Total Stipend

Selected fellows will receive a £10,000 total stipend for the 10-week programme.

This financial support is intended to support fellows while they participate in the full-time programme in Cambridge.

Expert Mentorship

Fellows will receive expert mentorship throughout the programme.

Mentorship can be particularly valuable for participants entering a new interdisciplinary field because it can help them understand the technical, scientific, policy and professional landscape surrounding AI and biosecurity.

Research Management

The programme provides research management support, which can help fellows structure and execute projects effectively.

This is particularly relevant to fellows working on complex questions that require interdisciplinary research and collaboration.

Workshops

Participants will have access to workshops designed to develop their knowledge and skills.

These workshops can provide opportunities to explore emerging issues and learn from experts working in relevant areas.

Networking

The fellowship provides networking opportunities with people working across AI, biology, biosecurity, policy, security and related fields.

For participants building careers in emerging interdisciplinary areas, these professional connections can be particularly valuable.

Operational Support

Fellows will also receive operational support, helping them focus on their projects and make productive use of the fellowship period.

Duration of the AIxBio Fellowship

The programme lasts for 10 weeks.

The 2027 fellowship is scheduled to run from:

18 January 2027 to 26 March 2027.

Participants are expected to take part in the programme on a full-time basis.

Location

The fellowship will be held in:

Cambridge, United Kingdom.

Because the programme is described as a full-time programme in Cambridge, prospective applicants should consider their ability to participate in person for the duration of the fellowship.

Eligibility Requirements

The AIxBio Fellowship has relatively broad eligibility requirements compared with many specialised research programmes.

Applicants must:

  • Be 18 years of age or older.
  • Have a strong interest in important problems at the intersection of AI and biosecurity.
  • Be able to participate in the 10-week full-time programme.
  • Be interested in contributing to efforts to reduce global catastrophic biological risks.

There are no other formal eligibility restrictions stated in the provided programme information.

Academic and Professional Backgrounds Welcomed

The fellowship welcomes applicants from multiple disciplines and career stages.

People with backgrounds in the following areas are specifically encouraged to apply:

Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning

AI and ML professionals can contribute technical expertise to questions involving advanced AI systems, AI safety and potential biological risks.

Software Engineering

Software engineers and technical professionals may be able to contribute to the development of tools, systems and approaches relevant to biosecurity and AI risk reduction.

Biology

Biologists can contribute scientific knowledge that helps bridge the gap between biological systems and advanced AI technologies.

Policy and Governance

Policy researchers and governance professionals can explore questions surrounding regulation, oversight, institutional responses and responsible development of emerging technologies.

Security

Security professionals may bring expertise in threat assessment, risk management and security systems.

Entrepreneurship

Founders and entrepreneurs can explore opportunities to create organisations, products or initiatives focused on addressing AI-biosecurity challenges.

Technically Minded Generalists

The programme also welcomes technically minded generalists who may not fit neatly into one conventional academic or professional category but can contribute valuable interdisciplinary skills.

Is the Fellowship Open to International Applicants?

The provided eligibility information does not specify a nationality or citizenship restriction.

It states that there are no other formal eligibility restrictions beyond being 18 or older.

Therefore, the programme is not presented as being restricted to applicants from a particular country, race or continent.

International applicants should, however, consider any applicable UK immigration, visa or travel requirements associated with participating in an in-person programme in Cambridge.

Why AI and Biosecurity Matter

The intersection between AI and biology is becoming increasingly important as artificial intelligence capabilities develop.

AI can potentially accelerate scientific discovery, improve analysis and support research. At the same time, increasingly capable technologies may create new challenges that need to be understood and managed.

The AIxBio Fellowship is focused on the risk-reduction side of this emerging field.

Its focus on global catastrophic biological risks means fellows can work on questions relating to how advanced technologies might interact with biological threats and how researchers, policymakers, security professionals and organisations can develop appropriate safeguards.

This makes the fellowship particularly relevant to individuals interested in the future of:

  • AI safety
  • Biological security
  • Technology governance
  • Global catastrophic risk reduction
  • Emerging technology policy
  • AI-enabled biological research
  • Security and risk management

How the Fellowship Can Support Career Development

The AIxBio Fellowship can provide participants with an opportunity to develop expertise in a rapidly emerging interdisciplinary field.

For researchers, it can provide a platform for developing new research ideas and expanding into AI-biosecurity.

For engineers and technical professionals, it can provide exposure to high-impact problems beyond conventional technology applications.

For policy professionals, it can provide an opportunity to engage with the governance challenges associated with emerging technologies.

For entrepreneurs, it can provide support for developing ideas addressing significant AI-biosecurity problems.

For graduate students and early-career professionals, the programme can provide exposure to experts and networks that may help shape future career directions.

How to Make Your Application Competitive

Although the programme does not require prior formal research experience, applicants should still demonstrate why they are well positioned to contribute.

Demonstrate a Clear Interest in AI and Biosecurity

Applicants should clearly explain why the intersection of artificial intelligence and biosecurity interests them.

A strong application should demonstrate that the applicant understands the importance of the field and has thought seriously about the problems they would like to address.

Highlight Relevant Skills

Applicants should identify technical, analytical, scientific, policy, security, research or entrepreneurial skills that could be useful during the fellowship.

Explain Your Motivation

Applicants should communicate why they want to participate and what they hope to accomplish during the 10-week programme.

Emphasise Interdisciplinary Thinking

AI-biosecurity problems often cross traditional disciplinary boundaries. Applicants should demonstrate an ability or willingness to work across fields.

Identify the Track That Best Fits Your Goals

Applicants should consider whether the Research, Placement or Founding Track best matches their experience and ambitions.

Focus on Impact

The fellowship is concerned with reducing potentially catastrophic biological risks. Applicants should therefore demonstrate how their interests, expertise or proposed work could contribute to meaningful risk reduction.

Key Fellowship Details at a Glance

Organisers ERA in partnership with the Cambridge Biosecurity Hub
Location Cambridge, United Kingdom
Duration 10 weeks
Dates 18 January – 26 March 2027
Stipend £10,000 total
Format Full-time
Age requirement 18+
Research experience Not formally required
Tracks Research, Placement and Founding

Application deadline 19 October 2026

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the AIxBio Fellowship 2027 is:

19 October 2026.

The programme is listed as closing soon, so interested applicants should begin preparing their applications as early as possible.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should apply through the official AIxBio Fellowship programme.

The opportunity page directs applicants to the programme’s official application and information platform.

Applicants should review the programme information carefully and ensure they understand the expectations of the 10-week full-time commitment before applying.

APPLY HERE

Important Considerations for International Applicants

Because the programme takes place in Cambridge, UK, international applicants should consider the practical requirements associated with participating in an in-person programme.

These may include:

  • Ability to travel to the United Kingdom.
  • Appropriate immigration or visa arrangements where applicable.
  • Availability for the full 10-week period.
  • Ability to participate full-time.
  • Accommodation and logistical arrangements in Cambridge.
  • Any other requirements communicated by the programme organisers.

The fellowship’s £10,000 stipend can provide financial support during the programme, but applicants should carefully review the official terms to understand precisely what expenses are covered.

Visit HERE for more information about the AIxBio Fellowship 2027 in Cambridge.

Conclusion

The AIxBio Fellowship 2027 is a distinctive opportunity for people who want to work on some of the most important emerging challenges at the intersection of advanced artificial intelligence and biosecurity.

Organised by ERA in partnership with the Cambridge Biosecurity Hub, the 10-week programme brings together researchers, engineers, policy professionals, security experts, entrepreneurs and other technically minded individuals to explore ways of reducing global catastrophic biological risks.

The programme offers a £10,000 total stipend, expert mentorship, research management, workshops, networking and operational support. Its three tracks — Research, Placement and Founding — allow participants with different professional goals to engage with the programme in ways suited to their backgrounds.

Another important feature is that prior formal research experience is not required, opening the opportunity to talented individuals who may have strong technical, professional, entrepreneurial or interdisciplinary capabilities without a conventional research background.

With the fellowship scheduled to run from 18 January to 26 March 2027 in Cambridge, UK, and applications closing on 19 October 2026, interested applicants should begin preparing their applications now.

For individuals passionate about artificial intelligence, biological security, emerging technology governance, AI safety, global catastrophic risk reduction or technology-driven solutions to major global challenges, the AIxBio Fellowship could provide an important platform for developing expertise, building networks and contributing to high-impact work in an increasingly important field.

item.content:encoded:
The UK Government, through the Government Economic Service (GES), offers university students an opportunity to gain practical experience in government economics through two student placement routes: the GES Summer Placement Scheme and the GES Sandwich Student Placement Scheme.

Both opportunities are designed for students in the penultimate year of an undergraduate degree who are interested in applying economics to real-world public policy challenges. The placements provide exposure to the work of government economists, allowing successful candidates to develop professional skills while contributing to work that supports government decision-making.

HM Treasury confirms that the Government Economic Service operates two centrally managed student work-experience schemes: a 6–12-week summer placement and a 12-month sandwich placement.

These opportunities can be particularly valuable for students who are considering a future career in economics, public policy, government analysis or the wider Civil Service.

1. HM Treasury Government Economic Service Summer Placement Scheme

The Government Economic Service Summer Placement Scheme is a paid short-term opportunity for eligible economics undergraduates who want to gain practical experience during the summer.

The scheme is intended for students who are considering a future career in the Government Economic Service after completing their studies.

According to the current GOV.UK information, the 2026 Summer Placement Scheme is open for applications from 1 October 2026 to 16 October 2026.

What is the Summer Placement Scheme?

The summer scheme allows successful students to spend 6 to 12 weeks working within the UK Civil Service during the summer period.

Rather than learning economics exclusively through lectures, textbooks and examinations, participants have the opportunity to apply their academic knowledge to practical issues facing government.

Students may work in government departments across the United Kingdom, with the exact locations and opportunities varying according to the participating departments and vacancies available during each recruitment round.

The experience can provide an important bridge between university study and a professional career in economics.

What can students gain from the summer placement?

A placement with the Government Economic Service can help students develop an understanding of how economics contributes to public policy.

Participants can gain experience in areas such as:

  • Applying economic theory to real-world policy questions
  • Understanding how government departments use economic evidence
  • Conducting economic analysis
  • Supporting policy development
  • Preparing analysis and briefings
  • Working with experienced economists
  • Understanding the Civil Service working environment
  • Developing professional communication skills
  • Building analytical and problem-solving abilities
  • Learning how economic evidence can influence government decisions

The experience is particularly useful for students who want to understand how economics works beyond the university classroom.

Click HERE for more information

2. HM Treasury Sandwich Student Placement Scheme

The second opportunity is the Government Economic Service Sandwich Student Placement Scheme.

Unlike the summer scheme, which lasts between six and twelve weeks, the sandwich placement provides an opportunity to spend approximately one year working in government before returning to university to complete an undergraduate degree.

The scheme is specifically aimed at economics undergraduates in their penultimate year.

Students spend the placement period working alongside experienced government economists and policy professionals before returning to their university studies.

A year of practical government experience

The sandwich scheme offers students a substantially longer period of professional experience than the summer programme.

During the placement, students can experience what it is like to work as part of a government economic team and contribute to policy-related work.

The opportunity is designed to connect academic economics with real government decision-making.

Students can potentially work on issues that have implications for public policy and society, while developing an understanding of how economic analysis is used within government.

The GES describes its sandwich scheme as an opportunity for students to spend a year working in a government department, learning about the role of economics in government and making a contribution to society.

Click HERE for more information

3. How the Two Opportunities Compare

Although both schemes are part of the Government Economic Service, they are designed around different placement lengths.

Feature Summer Placement Scheme Sandwich Student Placement
Organisation Government Economic Service Government Economic Service
Main institution UK Government/HM Treasury-led GES UK Government/HM Treasury-led GES
Duration 6–12 weeks Approximately 12 months
Timing Summer One academic placement year
Target students Penultimate-year economics undergraduates Penultimate-year economics undergraduates
Academic requirement On track for 2:1 or First Penultimate-year economics undergraduate; scheme-specific requirements apply
Purpose Short-term professional experience Extended professional placement
Paid Yes Yes
Location Government departments across the UK Government departments across the UK
Main focus Applying economics in practice Applying economics through a longer government placement

HM Treasury describes both routes as student work-experience schemes operated through the Government Economic Service.

4. Who Should Consider Applying?

These opportunities are particularly relevant to students who are interested in combining economics with public service.

They may appeal to students interested in:

  • Economics
  • Public policy
  • Government
  • Public finance
  • Economic development
  • Fiscal policy
  • Monetary and macroeconomic issues
  • Government decision-making
  • Evidence-based policy
  • Public administration
  • Economic research
  • Civil Service careers

For students considering a career as a government economist, the schemes can provide an opportunity to understand the profession before graduation.

The Government Economic Service also offers other routes into government economics, including graduate-level opportunities such as the Assistant Economist Scheme and Government Economic Service Fast Stream.

5. Summer Placement Eligibility Requirements

The Summer Placement Scheme has specific academic requirements.

According to the current GOV.UK guidance, applicants must be in the penultimate year of undergraduate study. This means that after completing the placement, the student must have one further year of university study remaining before completing their undergraduate degree.

Applicants must also be on track to achieve at least a 2:1 or First Class degree, based on their results so far.

Importantly, the economics requirement is specific.

Applicants must be studying one of the following:

  1. An undergraduate degree in Economics, either BA or BSc;
  2. An undergraduate joint degree containing Economics, where Economics represents at least 50% of the credit value of the modules studied and to be studied throughout the degree; or
  3. An undergraduate Philosophy, Politics and Economics (PPE) honours degree where Economics represents at least 50% of the relevant credit value.

Applicants must also have studied both microeconomics and macroeconomics.

Candidates must additionally satisfy the relevant UK immigration requirements and the Civil Service Nationality Rules. The Government Economic Service states that it does not provide visa sponsorship for these schemes.

6. Sandwich Placement Eligibility

The Sandwich Student Placement is also aimed at students in their penultimate year of undergraduate study.

The purpose of the placement is for students to spend a year working in government and then return to university to complete their degree.

This means applicants should not be students who are already completing their final year.

The GES describes its student schemes as routes specifically designed for students in their penultimate year of study.

As with the Summer Scheme, applicants must meet the applicable immigration and Civil Service nationality requirements, and the GES does not provide sponsorship for these schemes. Because eligibility conditions can differ between recruitment rounds and individual schemes, applicants should carefully review the official requirements before submitting an application.

7. Where Can Successful Students Work?

The opportunities are not necessarily restricted to HM Treasury itself.

The Government Economic Service supports economic work across different UK government departments. Civil Service information identifies organisations and departments where GES economists can work, including HM Treasury, HM Revenue & Customs, the Office for National Statistics, the Home Office and the Ministry of Justice.

The exact department and location available to a student can vary from one recruitment year to another.

The Summer Scheme guidance specifically states that opportunities are available in a range of government departments across the UK and that locations vary according to the department and year.

This means successful students may gain exposure to economic issues within different areas of government rather than working exclusively on one type of economic policy.

Click HERE for more information

8. Why This Experience Matters

One of the strongest features of these programmes is the opportunity to move from academic economics to practical economics.

At university, students may study economic models, theories, statistics, microeconomics and macroeconomics. A government placement provides an opportunity to see how this knowledge can be applied to real policy questions.

For example, economic analysis can help governments think about:

  • Public spending
  • Taxation
  • Economic growth
  • Employment
  • Government programmes
  • Public services
  • Investment
  • Business and economic development
  • The impact of policy decisions on households and businesses

Working within government can therefore help students understand the relationship between economic evidence, political priorities and public policy.

9. Professional Development

A placement can also help students develop skills that are valuable beyond economics.

These may include:

Analytical skills

Students can develop their ability to analyse information, interpret evidence and approach complex problems systematically.

Communication skills

Government economists need to communicate technical economic information clearly to policymakers and other audiences.

Policy understanding

Students can learn how evidence is incorporated into the policy-making process.

Teamwork

Working within a government department gives students experience collaborating with economists, civil servants, policy professionals and other specialists.

Professional experience

The placement provides experience within the Civil Service, helping students understand professional standards, organisational structures and government working environments.

Career exploration

The experience can also help students decide whether government economics is the right career path for them.

10. A Potential Pathway into a Government Economics Career

For students who want to become government economists, these programmes can form part of a broader career pathway.

The Government Economic Service operates several recruitment routes covering different stages of a person’s career. These include student schemes, graduate opportunities and other routes into the economics profession.

A student could therefore use a placement to gain practical experience and then explore graduate opportunities within the Government Economic Service after completing their degree.

The GES also has a Fast Stream and Assistant Economist Scheme for graduates.

11. Application Deadline

Summer Placement Scheme

For the 2026 Government Economic Service Summer Placement Scheme, applications are open from:

1 October 2026 to 16 October 2026.

Therefore, prospective applicants should ensure that they complete their application before 16 October 2026.

CLICK HERE TO APPLY FOR SUMMER PLACEMENT SCHEME

Sandwich Student Placement Scheme

The information provided for the Sandwich Student Placement Scheme does not state a specific application deadline.

The GES describes the Sandwich Scheme as an annual student recruitment route that opens in the autumn.

 CLICH HERE TO APPLY FOR THE SANDWICH STUDENT PLACEMENT SCHEME

Applicants should therefore check the official GES recruitment page for the current recruitment timetable and closing date before applying.

12. Important Information for International Students

International applicants should pay particular attention to the nationality and immigration requirements.

Although the schemes are advertised internationally and may be of interest to students studying outside the UK, eligibility is not determined simply by being an undergraduate student.

Candidates must meet the relevant Civil Service Nationality Rules and immigration requirements. The GES explicitly states that it does not offer visa sponsorship for these schemes.

Therefore, students who do not already have the necessary right to work in the UK should carefully examine the nationality and immigration requirements before investing time in an application.

 

13. Why Students Should Consider the Opportunity

The HM Treasury/Government Economic Service student schemes offer a combination of paid professional experience, exposure to government and practical application of economics.

For an eligible economics student, the opportunity can provide:

  • Real-world government experience
  • Paid employment during the placement
  • Exposure to experienced economists
  • Experience applying economics to policy
  • Professional networking
  • Development of analytical and communication skills
  • Understanding of Civil Service careers
  • Exposure to government departments
  • An opportunity to explore a long-term career in public-sector economics

The longer sandwich placement can be particularly valuable for students seeking substantial professional experience before graduating, while the summer scheme provides a shorter route for students who want to gain government experience without taking an entire year away from their studies.

14. Conclusion

The HM Treasury Government Economic Service Summer Placement Scheme and Sandwich Student Placement Scheme provide opportunities for eligible undergraduate economics students to experience how economics is applied within the UK Government.

The Summer Placement Scheme offers a paid 6–12-week experience during the summer, while the Sandwich Student Placement Scheme provides an opportunity to spend approximately one year working in government before returning to university.

Both schemes are designed to help students move beyond theoretical learning and understand how economic analysis contributes to real-world government decisions.

For the 2026 Summer Scheme, applications are open from 1 October to 16 October 2026, making the deadline particularly important for eligible students who wish to apply this year.

Students interested in a future career in government economics, public policy or the Civil Service should examine the eligibility criteria carefully and use the official Government Economic Service recruitment information when preparing their applications.

Who Can Apply?

Summer Placement Scheme

The primary eligible applicants are:

  • Undergraduate students in their penultimate year.
  • Students on track for a 2:1 or First Class degree.
  • Students studying Economics, an Economics joint degree with Economics comprising at least 50% of credits, or qualifying PPE degrees with Economics comprising at least 50%.
  • Applicants must have studied both microeconomics and macroeconomics.
  • Applicants must satisfy the relevant UK immigration and Civil Service Nationality Rules.

Sandwich Student Placement Scheme

The scheme is aimed at:

  • Undergraduate students in their penultimate year.
  • Students who will return to university after the placement to complete their degree.
  • Economics undergraduates meeting the specific GES requirements.
  • Applicants who satisfy the relevant UK immigration and Civil Service Nationality Rules.

Official Application Information

For more information on the government service summer scheme, click HERE

For more information on HM Treasury recruitment, click HERE

Nationality / Countries / Continent

There is no simple “open to all countries” rule for these schemes. Eligibility is governed by the UK Civil Service Nationality Rules and immigration requirements. The GES states that it does not provide visa sponsorship for these student schemes.

Therefore, applicants from Africa, Asia, Europe, the Americas or other regions should not assume that nationality alone makes them eligible. They must establish that they have the required nationality/immigration status and right to work under the applicable UK rules.

item.content:encoded:
The Sara E. and Bruce B. Collette Postdoctoral Fellowship in Systematic Ichthyology 2027 is offering an exceptional research opportunity for qualified early-career researchers seeking to undertake advanced, collections-based research on fish systematics at the Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History (NMNH) in the United States.

Supported through an endowed fellowship established by Bruce B. Collette and his wife, Sara, the programme is designed to support the next generation of researchers working in systematic ichthyology, particularly research involving comparative morphology and the study of fish collections.

The fellowship provides an opportunity for a postdoctoral researcher to conduct full-time, resident and independent research using the Smithsonian’s extensive fish collections, scientific facilities, library resources and expertise. The award is for one year, with the possibility of renewal.

Applications are open to both US and non-US citizens, making this a significant international postdoctoral opportunity for qualified researchers from around the world.

Sara E. and Bruce B. Collette Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027 at the Smithsonian

The fellowship was established in 2017 through the generous support of Bruce B. Collette, whose scientific career has focused extensively on collections-based systematic studies of marine fishes.

Dr. Collette began his career in 1960 and spent nearly six decades within the National Museum of Natural History community through his work with the National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) and NOAA, as well as through his affiliation with the Smithsonian.

His longstanding connection to the museum’s collections, library and scientific community inspired the creation of this fellowship.

The fellowship is intended to provide emerging researchers with an opportunity to experience and use the Smithsonian’s scientific collections and resources while contributing to the field of collections-based ichthyology.

The fellowship therefore combines advanced independent research, access to world-class scientific collections, mentorship and participation in a broader international research community.

Purpose of the Collette Postdoctoral Fellowship

The central purpose of the fellowship is to support full-time, resident, independent postdoctoral research in systematics, including comparative morphology, with a particular emphasis on using the fish collections held by the National Museum of Natural History.

The fellowship is particularly suited to researchers whose work can benefit substantially from the Smithsonian’s extensive collections and specialized research infrastructure.

Awardees are expected to become actively involved in the scholarly activities of the Division of Fishes and contribute to the broader field of collections-based systematic ichthyology at both national and international levels.

This means that the fellowship is not simply intended to provide financial support for independent research. It is designed to integrate fellows into a major scientific research environment where they can interact with researchers, collections specialists, curators and other members of the scientific community.

What Does the Fellowship Focus On?

The fellowship focuses on systematic ichthyology, the scientific study of fish diversity, classification, evolutionary relationships and related areas.

Research may involve areas such as:

  • Fish systematics
  • Comparative morphology
  • Taxonomic revisions
  • Phylogeny
  • Higher classification
  • Biogeography
  • Fish evolution
  • Osteology
  • Myology
  • Reproductive morphology
  • Larval fish studies
  • Ontogeny
  • Collections-based research
  • Comparative studies of fish specimens

Priority is given to proposals that clearly demonstrate how the researcher will use the Smithsonian’s fish collection and other resources to advance their research.

Research Opportunities at the Division of Fishes

The Smithsonian’s Division of Fishes provides an extensive scientific environment for researchers interested in fish systematics and related disciplines.

Current research activities include systematic revisions of species, genera and families, as well as research into higher classification and biogeography.

Research efforts have included work on:

  • Caribbean marine shorefish
  • Indo-Pacific marine shorefish
  • Beloniform fishes
  • Scombroid fishes
  • Pleuronectiform fishes
  • Tetraodontiform fishes
  • Larval fishes
  • Fish ontogeny
  • Reproductive morphology
  • Southeast Asian freshwater fishes
  • Phylogeny and higher classification

Researchers also have access to osteological, myological and other comparative studies that support the investigation of evolutionary relationships across a broad range of fish taxa.

Access to One of the World’s Largest Fish Collections

One of the major advantages of the Collette Postdoctoral Fellowship is access to the Smithsonian’s extensive Division of Fishes collection.

The collection contains more than 975,000 lots, representing more than 6 million individual fish specimens.

A “lot” refers to specimens of the same species collected at the same time and place.

The collection is organized phylogenetically by family and alphabetically by genus and species within each family. More than half of the collection has been computer catalogued and is available through an online searchable database.

The collection has particularly strong holdings of:

  • North American fishes
  • Neotropical fishes
  • Caribbean fishes
  • West Pacific fishes

This makes the fellowship particularly valuable for researchers whose projects require extensive comparative specimen-based research.

Additional Scientific Resources

Beyond the fish specimens themselves, fellows will have access to additional scientific resources that can support sophisticated research projects.

These resources include:

  • Illustrations and photographs of fishes
  • Radiographs
  • MicroCT facilities
  • Molecular laboratory facilities
  • Scanning electron microscopes
  • Digital imaging facilities
  • Radiographic systems
  • Light photography systems
  • Specialized research equipment
  • A dedicated fish research library
  • Extensive scientific reprints
  • Archives containing original illustrations, maps and photographs

The fish collection includes approximately 25,000 units of illustrations and photographs and approximately 25,000 radiographs.

The Division of Fishes library contains more than 8,000 volumes, together with an extensive collection of reprints and archives.

These resources can provide researchers with opportunities to conduct research that may not be possible using their home institution’s resources alone.

Fellowship Duration

The Collette Postdoctoral Fellowship is a one-year award.

The fellowship may be renewed, subject to the applicable conditions and review processes.

For the 2027 fellowship cycle, the eligible start-date window is:

  • Earliest start date: February 2, 2027
  • Latest start date: June 7, 2027

All formal requirements for the PhD must have been completed before the fellowship begins.

Fellowship Location

The fellowship is an in-person residential research opportunity.

The primary locations are:

National Museum of Natural History, Washington, DC

and

Museum Support Center, Suitland, Maryland

Because the fellowship is designed around direct access to the Smithsonian’s collections, laboratories, library and research community, applicants should be prepared to undertake their fellowship in person.

Financial Benefits and Award Package

The Collette Postdoctoral Fellowship provides a substantial financial package to support the fellow throughout the one-year research period.

The standard one-year award package includes:

$65,000 Annual Stipend

The fellow will receive a $65,000 annual stipend.

This provides the principal financial support for the one-year fellowship period.

$5,000 Research and Travel Allowance

The fellowship provides an additional $5,000 research/travel allowance.

This can support eligible research-related expenses and travel associated with the fellowship.

Applicants are encouraged to consider scientific meetings and opportunities to promote collections-based research when developing their research plans and budgets.

$5,000 Health Insurance Allowance

The fellowship includes a $5,000 health insurance allowance.

This contributes to eligible health insurance costs during the fellowship.

$1,000 Relocation Allowance

The award also includes a one-time $1,000 relocation allowance.

This is particularly relevant to fellows who need to relocate to the Washington, DC, or Suitland, Maryland, area for the fellowship.

Total Fellowship Package

The stated one-year award package totals $75,000, with an additional $1,000 in the first year for relocation, meaning the first-year financial package can amount to $76,000 when the relocation allowance is included.

Applicants should review the official fellowship terms carefully when preparing their financial plans.

Who Is Eligible for the Collette Postdoctoral Fellowship?

The fellowship is open to both US and non-US citizens.

Applicants should have a demonstrated record of research achievement and knowledge of the systematics of one or more groups of fishes.

In addition, applicants must have completed all formal requirements for their PhD before the start of the fellowship tenure.

The fellowship is therefore aimed at researchers who have already completed doctoral-level training and are ready to undertake independent postdoctoral research.

Key Eligibility Requirements

Applicants should:

  • Be a US or non-US citizen.
  • Hold a PhD or have completed all formal PhD requirements before the fellowship begins.
  • Have a demonstrated record of research accomplishment.
  • Have knowledge of the systematics of one or more groups of fishes.
  • Be prepared to conduct full-time, resident research.
  • Have a research project appropriate for the fellowship.
  • Be able to make meaningful use of the Smithsonian’s fish collections and associated research resources.

Priority Will Be Given to Strong Research Proposals

Although the fellowship is open to eligible applicants internationally, the Smithsonian has identified particular characteristics that will receive priority during consideration.

Priority will be given to proposals that:

  1. Focus on systematic ichthyology

    Research should have a strong connection to systematic ichthyology and related areas of fish systematics.

  2. Demonstrate high research productivity and creativity

    Applicants should demonstrate their ability to conduct high-quality research and contribute innovative ideas to their field.

  3. Demonstrate strong potential for interaction

    The proposed work should show potential for scholarly interaction and engagement within the Division of Fishes and the broader research community.

  4. Make meaningful use of Smithsonian collections

    Applicants should clearly explain why the Smithsonian’s fish collections and other NMNH resources are important to their research.

The last point is particularly important. Applicants should not simply propose a project that could be conducted anywhere. The proposal should demonstrate why conducting the research at the Smithsonian is scientifically valuable.

Application Materials

Applicants must submit their applications through the Smithsonian’s Online Application System (SOLAA).

The application must include several important components.

1. Curriculum Vitae

Applicants must submit a CV containing relevant information such as:

  • Education
  • Areas of expertise
  • Research achievements
  • Honors
  • Publications
  • Research interests

The CV should provide a clear picture of the applicant’s research background and academic accomplishments.

2. Recent Publications

Applicants may submit a maximum of three PDF publications.

These publications should help demonstrate the applicant’s research productivity, expertise and ability to contribute to the proposed area of study.

3. Research Proposal

Applicants must provide a research proposal consisting of:

  • Abstract
  • Research statement
  • Timetable
  • Budget

The research proposal is one of the most important components of the application because it enables reviewers to assess the scientific value, feasibility and relevance of the proposed research.

4. Two Letters of Reference

Applicants must arrange for two letters of reference.

The referees should be individuals who are familiar with the applicant’s work.

The referees are expected to submit their letters separately through the online application system.

Applicants are responsible for ensuring that the letters are submitted by the deadline.

Research Proposal Requirements

The research proposal must be carefully structured and address the specific requirements outlined by the Smithsonian.

Abstract

The proposal must include an abstract of the proposed research.

The abstract is limited to 250 words.

Applicants should use the abstract to clearly communicate the research question, approach and significance of the proposed project.

Full Research Proposal

The full research statement should describe the research planned for the one-year fellowship.

It should address:

  • Research methodology
  • Importance of the research
  • Relevance to the broader discipline
  • Importance of the research to the applicant’s scholarly development
  • Reasons for conducting the research at the Smithsonian
  • How the applicant will use resources in the Department of Vertebrate Zoology and Division of Fishes

The research proposal is limited to three double-spaced pages, including figures, using 11-point type.

Timetable

Applicants must provide a detailed timetable showing how they intend to accomplish their research objectives during the one-year fellowship.

The timetable should include:

  • Major research milestones
  • Expected stages of the project
  • Estimated travel dates
  • Important activities required to complete the research

A realistic timetable can demonstrate that the proposed project is achievable within the fellowship period.

Budget and Justification

Applicants must provide a detailed budget and justification covering items such as:

  • Equipment
  • Supplies
  • Research-related travel
  • Other research support

The budget should exclude the stipend and relocation costs.

Applicants are strongly encouraged to consider including travel to scientific meetings and activities that promote collections-based research.

Where possible, applicants are also encouraged to discuss anticipated research expenses with NMNH staff before submitting their application.

If the proposed research requires funding beyond the $5,000 annual research allowance, applicants should explain where the additional funding would come from.

Bibliography

Applicants should provide a bibliography of literature relevant to their proposed research where necessary.

The bibliography is limited to two pages.

References

Applicants must provide the names and email addresses of the two individuals who will submit letters of reference.

Applicants are encouraged to provide their referees with a copy of the research proposal so that the references can be prepared appropriately.

Applicants should also follow up with referees to ensure that their letters are submitted before the application deadline.

Identifying an Advisor

A particularly important component of the application is identifying an appropriate fellowship advisor.

Applicants must identify:

  • One member of the NMNH Fish Division staff or affiliated staff, including retirees, to serve as their principal fellowship advisor.
  • A second person to serve as an alternate or co-advisor.

This means prospective applicants should carefully examine the research interests and expertise of Smithsonian Fish Division personnel and identify researchers whose expertise aligns with their proposed project.

Establishing this alignment can help applicants demonstrate that their project fits within the scientific environment and resources of the Smithsonian.

How to Apply for the Smithsonian Collette Fellowship

Applications must be submitted through the Smithsonian’s SOLAA online application system.

Applicants should follow these steps:

Step 1: Create an Account or Log In

Applicants should create a SOLAA account or log into an existing account.

Step 2: Start the Application

After logging in, select the option to Start Application.

Step 3: Select the Institution

Select:

NMNH – National Museum of Natural History

as the Office/Museum/Research Center.

Step 4: Search for the Fellowship

Search for:

Collette Postdoctoral Fellowship in Systematic Ichthyology

Step 5: Select “Apply Now”

Once the programme is located, select Apply Now and proceed with the application.

Applicants should ensure that all required documents are uploaded and that reference letters are submitted before the closing deadline.

APPLY HERE

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the Sara E. and Bruce B. Collette Postdoctoral Fellowship in Systematic Ichthyology is:

November 20, 2026, at 11:59 PM EST.

Applicants should not wait until the final hours to submit their applications because they need to allow sufficient time for uploading documents and ensuring that their two referees submit their recommendation letters.

Fellowship Start Dates

Successful applicants should be prepared to begin the fellowship within the designated start-date window.

The fellowship may begin as early as:

February 2, 2027

and no later than:

June 7, 2027.

All formal PhD requirements must be completed before the start of the fellowship.

Previous Fellowship Awardees

The programme has already supported researchers who have gone on to develop careers in ichthyology and museum-based research.

The first fellowship was awarded in 2018 to William B. Ludt, PhD, of Louisiana State University.

In September 2019, Ludt began serving as an Assistant Curator of Ichthyology at the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County.

The second fellowship was awarded in 2019 to Murilo Pastana, PhD, of the Museu de Zoologia da Universidade de São Paulo.

In January 2023, Pastana began serving as a Curator of Fishes at MZUSP.

These examples demonstrate the potential of the fellowship to support researchers pursuing long-term careers in ichthyology, natural history collections and museum-based scientific research.

Why This Fellowship Is a Significant Opportunity for Researchers

The Collette Postdoctoral Fellowship offers several advantages beyond its financial package.

Access to Exceptional Scientific Collections

Researchers gain access to one of the world’s largest comparative fish collections, containing millions of individual specimens.

International Research Environment

The fellowship brings researchers into the Smithsonian’s international scientific community and provides opportunities for scholarly interaction.

Advanced Research Infrastructure

Access to specialized equipment and facilities can support sophisticated research methodologies.

Professional Development

Participation in the Division of Fishes can help fellows expand their professional networks and develop relationships with researchers in their field.

Independent Research

The programme is designed around independent postdoctoral research, allowing fellows to develop and execute a substantial research project.

Potential Career Development

The careers of previous fellows demonstrate how specialized postdoctoral training and access to major natural history collections can contribute to future academic and museum-based careers.

Visit HERE for more information about the Smithsonian Collette Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027.

How Applicants Can Strengthen Their Applications

Because this is a specialized postdoctoral fellowship, applicants should ensure that their applications demonstrate a strong connection between their research and the programme’s priorities.

Make the Smithsonian Connection Clear

Do not simply describe a research project in general terms. Explain specifically why the NMNH Division of Fishes collection is necessary or particularly valuable for the proposed work.

Demonstrate Research Productivity

Use the CV and publications to demonstrate your research achievements, scholarly expertise and contributions to systematic ichthyology.

Develop a Focused Research Question

The research proposal should have a clear scientific question and demonstrate a logical methodology for addressing it.

Explain the Broader Importance

Applicants should explain why the research matters to systematic ichthyology and the broader scientific community.

Identify Appropriate Advisors

Research the expertise of Fish Division staff and affiliated researchers before identifying a principal advisor and alternate or co-advisor.

Build a Realistic Budget

Ensure that the proposed research expenses are realistic and clearly justified. If costs are expected to exceed the $5,000 research allowance, explain the anticipated source of additional funding.

Start Early

Because two external reference letters are required, applicants should contact potential referees well before the deadline and give them sufficient time to prepare and submit their letters.

Conclusion

The Sara E. and Bruce B. Collette Postdoctoral Fellowship in Systematic Ichthyology 2027 is a highly specialized opportunity for researchers seeking to advance their careers in fish systematics, taxonomy, comparative morphology and collections-based ichthyological research.

With a $65,000 annual stipend, $5,000 research and travel allowance, $5,000 health insurance allowance and a $1,000 relocation allowance, the fellowship provides substantial support for a one-year period of full-time research at the Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History.

More importantly, fellows gain access to an exceptional scientific environment, including a fish collection containing more than 6 million individual specimens, specialized laboratories and imaging facilities, extensive scientific literature and the expertise of researchers within the Smithsonian’s Division of Fishes.

The fellowship is open to US and international applicants, making it a valuable opportunity for qualified researchers around the world. However, applicants should ensure that their proposed research strongly aligns with systematic ichthyology and demonstrates a clear reason for using the Smithsonian’s collections and research infrastructure.

With the application deadline set for November 20, 2026, at 11:59 PM EST, eligible researchers should begin preparing their CV, publications, research proposal, budget, timetable and reference letters well in advance. A strong application should clearly demonstrate research excellence, originality, scientific relevance and the specific value of conducting the proposed research at the Smithsonian.

item.content:encoded:
The Kaduna Youth Policy Lab 2026 is inviting young people in Kaduna State, Nigeria, who are passionate about governance, public policy, accountability and social change to apply for a practical training and mentorship programme designed to develop the next generation of youth policy analysts.

The programme will equip selected participants with practical skills in policy analysis, policy research, policy writing, budget literacy and evidence-based advocacy. Participants will also have an opportunity to work collaboratively with other young people, develop policy briefs and engage with government institutions on governance and public policy issues.

With only 25 participants set to be selected, the Kaduna Youth Policy Lab 2026 offers a focused opportunity for young people who want to better understand how policy decisions are made and how evidence, data and technology can be used to promote accountable governance and meaningful social change.

About the Kaduna Youth Policy Lab 2026

The Kaduna Youth Policy Lab 2026 is designed as a practical learning and engagement programme for young people interested in the intersection of youth participation, governance, public policy, data, accountability and community development.

Rather than focusing solely on theoretical learning, the programme is structured around practical activities that can help participants understand how policy research and advocacy work in real-world settings.

Participants will take part in a two-day non-residential policy bootcamp, receive mentorship, collaborate in teams and work towards producing policy briefs addressing governance and policy challenges relevant to Kaduna State.

The programme also includes opportunities for participants to participate in advocacy engagements with government institutions, giving young people exposure to how policy discussions can connect with public institutions and decision-makers.

What Will Participants Gain?

Selected participants will have the opportunity to develop a range of practical skills and experiences relevant to careers in public policy, governance, research, advocacy, development and civic engagement.

1. Two-Day Policy Bootcamp

Participants will participate in an intensive two-day policy bootcamp designed to strengthen their understanding of policy-related issues and provide practical learning opportunities.

The bootcamp is expected to provide a collaborative environment where young people can learn, exchange ideas and apply policy concepts to real governance challenges.

2. Policy Research and Analysis Skills

The programme will help participants strengthen their ability to conduct policy research and analyse governance-related issues.

These skills can be particularly valuable for young people interested in careers or further studies involving:

  • Public policy
  • Governance
  • Development
  • Political science
  • International development
  • Research
  • Advocacy
  • Public administration
  • Civil society
  • Government and public institutions

3. Policy Writing Experience

Participants will gain practical exposure to policy writing, including working with other participants to develop policy briefs.

A policy brief is an important tool for communicating research and evidence to policymakers and other stakeholders. Learning how to identify a policy problem, examine evidence and formulate practical recommendations can therefore be valuable for anyone interested in influencing public policy.

4. Mentorship

The Kaduna Youth Policy Lab will provide participants with mentorship opportunities, allowing them to learn from individuals with relevant knowledge and experience.

Mentorship can help young participants better understand policy careers, advocacy, research and approaches to addressing governance challenges.

5. Teamwork and Collaboration

Participants will work with other young people during the programme, including collaborating on policy briefs.

This will provide an opportunity to strengthen skills such as

  • Teamwork
  • Communication
  • Problem-solving
  • Research collaboration
  • Leadership
  • Critical thinking
  • Stakeholder engagement

6. Advocacy Engagements

Participants will have the opportunity to take part in advocacy engagements with government institutions.

This component can give young people practical exposure to government engagement and demonstrate how evidence and policy recommendations can be communicated to public institutions.

7. Understanding of Budget Literacy and Accountability

The programme specifically seeks to build skills around budget literacy and accountable governance.

Understanding public budgets is important because government budgets influence the resources available for public services, development programmes and community priorities.

Young people who develop budget literacy can become better equipped to examine public expenditure, ask informed questions and participate constructively in discussions about government accountability.

Policy Issues Participants Can Explore

Applicants are asked to indicate the governance or policy issue that interests them most.

The available areas include:

Youth Employment and Economic Opportunities

Youth employment is an important policy issue, particularly in relation to access to decent work, entrepreneurship, skills development and economic opportunities.

Participants interested in this area may explore policies affecting young people’s participation in the economy and potential approaches to expanding employment and livelihood opportunities.

Education Financing and Accountability

Education financing and accountability focus on how resources are allocated to education and how stakeholders can promote transparency and effective use of public resources.

This area may appeal to applicants interested in education policy, public finance, access to education and accountability.

Public Expenditure and Budget Transparency

This area focuses on understanding how public resources are allocated and spent.

Applicants interested in public financial management can use the programme as an opportunity to develop their understanding of budgets, expenditure and transparency.

Local Government Accountability and Service Delivery

Local governments play an important role in delivering services and responding to community needs.

Participants interested in this area may explore how local government institutions can improve accountability, responsiveness and service delivery.

AI Governance and Data-Driven Public Policy

The programme also highlights the growing importance of Artificial Intelligence and data-driven tools in policy analysis and governance.

Applicants are specifically asked to explain how AI and data-driven tools can contribute to policy analysis, good governance and social change in Kaduna State.

This makes the programme particularly relevant to young people interested in the intersection of technology, artificial intelligence, data and public policy.

Who Can Apply?

The Kaduna Youth Policy Lab 2026 is intended for young people residing in Kaduna State, Nigeria, particularly those who have an interest in governance, public policy and creating positive change in their communities.

Applicants should demonstrate an interest in issues such as governance, policy, accountability, research, advocacy, leadership or social change.

The application form asks applicants to provide information including:

  • Full name
  • Email address
  • Age
  • Gender
  • Residence within Kaduna City
  • Current occupation
  • Institution or organization
  • Previous experience
  • Policy interests
  • Motivation for joining the programme
  • Expected learning outcomes
  • Availability for the two-day bootcamp
  • Willingness to work in a team
  • Willingness to participate in a government advocacy visit
  • Accessibility support requirements

The programme will select only 25 participants, making it important for applicants to complete the application carefully and provide clear, thoughtful responses.

Previous Experience Is Not the Only Consideration

The application asks whether applicants have previous experience in community engagement, advocacy, research or leadership.

Applicants who answer yes are asked to briefly describe their experience.

However, the application also allows applicants to indicate that they do not have previous experience. This means applicants should carefully answer the question honestly rather than assuming that they need extensive professional experience to apply.

Young people who have participated in community activities, student leadership, volunteer initiatives, research projects, advocacy campaigns or other forms of civic engagement may wish to explain these experiences clearly.

AI, Data and the Future of Public Policy

One of the distinctive elements of the Kaduna Youth Policy Lab 2026 is its emphasis on Artificial Intelligence and data-driven tools.

Applicants are asked how AI and data-driven tools can contribute to policy analysis, good governance and social change in Kaduna State.

This question gives applicants an opportunity to demonstrate their understanding of how technology can support evidence-based decision-making.

For example, AI and data tools can potentially support policy work by helping stakeholders:

  • Analyse large volumes of information.
  • Identify trends and patterns in datasets.
  • Support evidence-based research.
  • Improve access to information.
  • Identify emerging social and economic issues.
  • Support monitoring and evaluation.
  • Improve public service planning.
  • Strengthen data-informed decision-making.

However, responsible use of AI also requires attention to issues such as data privacy, accuracy, bias, transparency, accountability and human oversight.

Applicants may therefore want to demonstrate a balanced understanding of both the opportunities and responsibilities associated with using AI in public policy.

Application Questions

Applicants will be required to respond to a series of questions designed to assess their background, interests, motivation and availability.

Some of the key questions include:

  1. Why do you want to join the Kaduna Youth Policy Lab 2026?
  2. How do you think AI and data-driven tools can contribute to policy analysis, good governance and social change in Kaduna State?
  3. Which governance or policy issue interests you most?
  4. Do you have previous experience in community engagement, advocacy, research or leadership?
  5. What do you hope to learn from the programme?
  6. Are you available to participate in the two-day non-residential bootcamp?
  7. Are you willing to work with a team to develop a policy brief?
  8. Are you willing to participate in a government advocacy visit?
  9. Do you require any accessibility support to participate?

Applicants should take time to provide thoughtful and specific responses rather than submitting generic statements.

How to Strengthen Your Application

Because only 25 participants will be selected, applicants should make their responses as relevant and compelling as possible.

Demonstrate Your Interest in Governance

Explain what attracts you to governance and public policy and, where possible, connect your interest to a specific issue affecting communities in Kaduna State.

Be Specific About Your Motivation

Instead of simply stating that you want to “gain experience,” explain what you hope to learn and how you intend to use those skills after completing the programme.

Highlight Relevant Experience

If you have participated in research, student leadership, community initiatives, volunteering, advocacy, civic activities or other projects, briefly explain what you did and what you learned.

Connect Technology to Policy

Since the application specifically asks about AI and data-driven tools, applicants should demonstrate an understanding of how technology can support evidence-based policymaking while acknowledging the importance of responsible and ethical use.

Demonstrate Your Willingness to Collaborate

The programme involves teamwork and development of policy briefs. Applicants should therefore demonstrate that they are comfortable working with people who may have different perspectives and experiences.

Show Your Interest in Practical Impact

Strong applicants can explain how they would use the knowledge gained from the programme to contribute to their community, professional development or future policy and advocacy work.

Programme Participation Requirements

Applicants should carefully consider the practical participation requirements before applying.

Selected participants are expected to:

  • Be available for the two-day non-residential bootcamp.
  • Work collaboratively with other participants.
  • Contribute to the development of a policy brief.
  • Participate in relevant advocacy activities.
  • Be willing to engage with government institutions as part of the programme.
  • Provide complete and accurate information in the application form.

Applicants can also indicate whether they require accessibility support to participate.

Number of Participants

The Kaduna Youth Policy Lab 2026 is a selective programme.

Only 25 participants will be selected.

This limited cohort is likely to allow for a more focused learning environment, closer collaboration among participants and practical engagement around policy issues.

Application Deadline

Deadline: Not specified in the information provided.

Applicants should therefore check the official application form or programme announcement for any deadline or closing date before submitting their application.

APPLY HERE

How to Apply

Interested young people should complete the online application form and provide all the required information.

The application form is hosted on Google Forms and asks applicants to provide personal information, educational or occupational details, their policy interests, relevant experience, motivation and availability.

Applicants should carefully review all responses before submitting because the programme states that only 25 participants will be selected.

Visit HERE for more information about the Kaduna Youth Policy Lab 2026.

Conclusion

The Kaduna Youth Policy Lab 2026 presents an opportunity for young people in Kaduna State to strengthen their understanding of public policy, governance, accountability and evidence-based advocacy while developing practical research and policy-writing skills.

Through the two-day policy bootcamp, mentorship, teamwork, policy brief development and government advocacy engagements, participants will have the opportunity to move beyond theoretical discussions and gain practical exposure to policy processes.

The programme’s focus on AI, data-driven policy analysis, budget literacy, public expenditure, local government accountability, education financing and youth economic opportunities also makes it particularly relevant to young people interested in the future of governance and evidence-based decision-making.

With only 25 participants to be selected, eligible young people who are passionate about improving governance and creating positive change in their communities should prepare their applications carefully and clearly demonstrate their motivation, policy interests, relevant experiences and commitment to participating in the full programme.

For more global Training opportunities, visit OFY HERE.
