item.content:encoded:
The IATSS Forum 2027 is inviting applications from young professionals and emerging leaders who are interested in developing their leadership capabilities, exchanging knowledge across cultures and contributing to sustainable development in their countries and the wider Asian region.

The programme is designed around the idea of co-creative and collaborative leadership, bringing together professionals from different countries, cultures, professional backgrounds and areas of expertise. Participants are expected not only to learn from the programme but also to share their own experiences, knowledge, perspectives and professional expertise with other participants.

For 2027, the programme will be conducted through two possible eight-week sessions: the 71st IATSS Forum from May to July 2027 and the 72nd IATSS Forum from September to November 2027. Applicants should note that the programme schedule and timeframe may be subject to change, and applicants cannot guarantee or select which programme period they will ultimately be assigned to.

The IATSS Forum is particularly interested in individuals who have demonstrated leadership experience, understand the challenges facing their communities and countries, possess a strong desire to create positive change, and have the potential to use the knowledge and networks gained through the programme for the benefit of society.

IATSS Forum 2027 Programme Overview

The IATSS Forum is structured as an intensive international learning and leadership development experience. It provides participants with an opportunity to step outside their usual professional and cultural environments and engage with people from different backgrounds.

The programme places particular importance on:

  • Leadership development
  • Cross-cultural understanding
  • Collaborative and co-creative leadership
  • Sustainable regional development
  • Knowledge and experience sharing
  • Professional and personal development
  • Understanding social and regional challenges
  • Building international networks
  • Learning from people with different professional and cultural perspectives
  • Developing the ability to contribute to communities and society

Participants are expected to actively engage in lectures, group discussions, meetings, learning activities, and other programme components.

The programme is therefore intended for individuals who are not simply looking to attend an international programme, but who have a clear idea of how the experience can contribute to their future leadership journey and their ability to create positive change.

IATSS Forum 2027 Programme Dates

The 2027 programme is currently scheduled across two possible eight-week periods.

71st IATSS Forum

May to July 2027

Duration: 8 weeks

72nd IATSS Forum

September to November 2027

Duration: 8 weeks

Applicants should be aware that the programme schedule and timeframe are subject to change.

In addition, applicants cannot guarantee which of the two programme periods they will be assigned to. Selection for the programme therefore does not necessarily mean that an applicant will be able to choose between the May–July and September–November sessions.

Application Deadline for IATSS Forum 2027

The application period for the 2027 IATSS Forum runs from:

1 June 2026 to 30 September 2026

Application Deadline: 30 September 2026

Applicants are strongly encouraged to begin preparing their documents well before the deadline. The application requires several documents, including an application form, basic question form, essay, recommendation form, and, where applicable, proof of English proficiency.

Because some documents may require coordination with an employer or direct supervisor, applicants should avoid waiting until the final days of the application period.

Applications must be submitted through the designated online application process. Submissions by email are not accepted.

Who Is the IATSS Forum Looking For?

The IATSS Forum has outlined several characteristics that it considers important when selecting candidates.

The selection process is not based solely on academic qualifications or professional experience. Instead, the programme seeks individuals who demonstrate leadership potential, awareness of social and community issues, a willingness to learn from others, and a clear motivation to contribute to sustainable development.

The ideal candidate should be able to demonstrate several of the following qualities.

  1. Leadership Experience and Potential

Leadership is one of the central qualities sought by the IATSS Forum.

Candidates should ideally have experience leading a team within an organisation or professional environment. However, leadership is not presented simply as holding a formal managerial position.

The programme is interested in individuals who understand their own leadership strengths as well as the areas where they need to improve.

Applicants should therefore be able to reflect on questions such as:

  • What type of leader am I?
  • What leadership responsibilities have I undertaken?
  • What have I learned from leading others?
  • What challenges have I encountered as a leader?
  • What areas of my leadership skills still need development?
  • How do I work with people who have different perspectives from my own?

The IATSS Forum places particular emphasis on co-creative and collaborative leadership.

This means that effective leadership is understood as the ability to bring together people with different experiences, cultures, professional backgrounds, and perspectives and work collectively towards a shared objective.

Candidates should therefore demonstrate an ability and willingness to collaborate rather than relying solely on individual leadership.

  1. Co-Creative and Collaborative Leadership

A major focus of the IATSS Forum is the concept of co-creative/collaborative leadership.

Participants will come from different cultural and professional environments. This diversity is viewed as an opportunity for learning and collective problem-solving.

Candidates should understand that leadership can involve:

  • Listening to different perspectives
  • Respecting cultural differences
  • Building consensus
  • Encouraging participation
  • Recognizing the strengths of team members
  • Combining different areas of expertise
  • Working towards common goals
  • Learning from people with different experiences
  • Creating solutions collectively

The programme therefore seeks people who can contribute to a diverse learning environment while also learning from others.

  1. Awareness of Issues Facing Their Country and Community

Another important characteristic is awareness of the challenges facing the applicant’s own country and community.

Candidates should have an understanding of important social, economic, environmental, institutional, developmental, or other challenges relevant to their communities.

However, awareness alone is not sufficient.

The IATSS Forum is looking for people who have the motivation to take on a leadership role in addressing these challenges.

Applicants should be able to demonstrate that they are not merely observers of problems but are interested in becoming part of the process of creating solutions.

This could involve professional work, community engagement, social initiatives, organisational leadership, public policy, development work, business, education, civil society, or other forms of contribution.

  1. Commitment to Sustainable Development

The programme seeks candidates who are motivated to contribute to the future sustainable development of the region.

Applicants should therefore consider how their professional work and leadership can contribute to long-term positive change.

This can include developing solutions to challenges affecting communities, improving institutions, supporting inclusive development, strengthening cooperation, or using professional expertise to address problems facing society.

Candidates should have a clear understanding of why sustainable development matters to their country and region and how they hope to contribute.

  1. Broad Skills, Experience and Expertise

The IATSS Forum brings together participants with different professional backgrounds and areas of expertise.

Candidates are therefore expected to possess a broad range of skills, experience, and professional knowledge that can be shared with other participants.

Applicants should consider what unique perspectives they can bring to the programme.

This could include expertise gained through:

  • Professional employment
  • Leadership responsibilities
  • Community initiatives
  • Policy work
  • Research
  • Business
  • Civil society
  • Development programmes
  • Education
  • Public administration
  • Social entrepreneurship
  • Technology
  • Environmental initiatives
  • International cooperation
  • Other professional or community-based activities

The important point is that participants should be able to contribute knowledge and experience to discussions and group learning.

  1. Strong English Communication Skills

English proficiency is an important requirement because the programme involves active participation in an international environment.

Candidates should have sufficient English skills to participate effectively in:

  • Lectures
  • Group discussions
  • Meetings
  • Knowledge-sharing sessions
  • Collaborative activities
  • Cross-cultural exchanges

Participants are expected not simply to understand English but to be able to communicate their experiences, knowledge, opinions, and ideas to people from different backgrounds.

Applicants may submit a certificate demonstrating English proficiency, where applicable.

Accepted examples listed in the application information include certificates such as:

  • TOEFL
  • TOEIC
  • Other relevant English proficiency certificates

An English proficiency certificate should be attached if applicable.

  1. Potential for Personal and Professional Development

The IATSS Forum recognises that strong candidates may not already possess every skill required to achieve their long-term goals.

The programme is therefore also interested in candidates who have the potential to gain what they currently lack through participation.

Applicants should be able to identify areas where they want to grow.

For example, a candidate may want to improve:

  • Leadership abilities
  • Cross-cultural communication
  • Collaborative problem-solving
  • Strategic thinking
  • International networking
  • Professional communication
  • Understanding of regional issues
  • Team management
  • Intercultural collaboration
  • Ability to develop sustainable solutions

The key is demonstrating how participation in the IATSS Forum can help the applicant become a more effective professional and leader.

  1. Independence and Adaptability

The programme takes place in a diversified international environment.

Candidates should therefore be disciplined, independent, adaptable, and comfortable learning alongside people with different cultural and professional backgrounds.

Applicants should demonstrate:

  • Independence
  • Responsibility
  • Adaptability
  • Respect for different cultures
  • Openness to learning
  • Positive engagement with others
  • Willingness to work in diverse teams

Participants should also possess the physical and mental capabilities necessary to fully participate in programme activities without an accompanying person.

  1. Respect for Diversity and Other Perspectives

The IATSS Forum is built around interaction among people from different backgrounds.

Candidates should therefore demonstrate a positive attitude towards learning from and respecting others.

This means being willing to encounter perspectives that may differ significantly from one’s own.

Successful participants are expected to:

  • Listen actively
  • Respect different viewpoints
  • Engage constructively in discussions
  • Avoid dismissing unfamiliar perspectives
  • Learn from cultural differences
  • Share their own experiences respectfully
  • Work collaboratively with people from different backgrounds

This intercultural dimension is an important part of the programme experience.

 

  1. Clear Goals for Participating in the IATSS Forum

Applicants should be able to clearly explain what they hope to gain from participating in the programme.

A strong application should therefore connect the applicants:

Current experience → Leadership goals → Learning needs → IATSS Forum experience → Future contribution

Candidates should have a clear understanding of why the programme is relevant to their professional and personal development.

They should also demonstrate that their goals are aligned with the contents and philosophy of the IATSS Forum.

IATSS Forum 2027 Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must meet the programme’s eligibility requirements.

Nationality

Applicants must possess the nationality of one of the following countries:

  1. Cambodia
  2. India
  3. Indonesia
  4. Laos
  5. Malaysia
  6. Myanmar
  7. Philippines
  8. Singapore
  9. Thailand
  10. Vietnam

Age

Applicants must be 35 years old or younger as of the application closing date.

Since the application deadline is 30 September 2026, applicants must meet the age requirement as of that date.

Current Employment

Applicants must currently be working as a full-time employee in a professional field.

The eligibility information also states that:

  • Self-employed applicants can apply.
  • Freelancers can apply.

Therefore, the requirement is focused on current professional engagement rather than exclusively requiring employment by a traditional organisation.

Professional Experience

Applicants should have at least two years of full-time professional job experience at the time of application.

Candidates should therefore be able to demonstrate meaningful professional experience and explain how that experience has contributed to their leadership development and understanding of issues in their community or country.

English Ability

Applicants should have sufficient English proficiency to live and study abroad and actively participate in the programme.

English will be particularly important for lectures, discussions, meetings, presentations, and interaction with other participants.

Cultural Adaptability

Applicants should have sufficient cultural adaptability to live and study abroad.

The programme involves interaction with people from different cultural and professional backgrounds, making openness, adaptability, respect, and intercultural communication important qualities.

Ability to Participate Independently

Applicants must possess the physical and mental capabilities necessary to fully participate in programme activities without an accompanying person.

Candidates should therefore be prepared to participate independently in the full range of programme activities.

How the IATSS Forum 2027 Application Process Works

Applications are accepted once a year.

The selection process consists of two main stages:

  1. Document-based screening
  2. Interview-based screening

Only shortlisted applicants will be invited for an interview.

The interview schedule varies depending on the applicant’s country. Applicants should therefore understand that the interview date and time may differ between countries.

Only applicants who are shortlisted will receive notification regarding the interview.

For more information, please CLICK HERE

 

Documents Required for the IATSS Forum Application

Applicants must submit all required documents through the online application page.

The required documents include the following.

  1. Application Form

Applicants must complete the official Application Form provided by the IATSS Forum.

The form can be completed using:

  • Microsoft Word, or
  • PDF

Applicants should ensure that all information is complete and accurate before converting and submitting the final document.

CLICK HERE

 

  1. Basic Question Form

Applicants must complete the Basic Question Form provided as part of the application materials.

The application booklet contains instructions explaining how applicants should approach the questions.

Applicants should carefully read these instructions before completing the form.

Importantly, the IATSS Forum explicitly states that submitting AI-generated text for the Basic Question Form will result in immediate disqualification.

Applicants should therefore write their answers themselves and ensure that their responses genuinely reflect their own experiences, perspectives, motivations, and goals.

  1. Essay

Applicants must also write a short essay on the topic provided in the official application materials.

The essay must be completed using the designated form and should follow the instructions contained in the Application Booklet.

As with the Basic Question Form, applicants are explicitly warned that AI-generated text submitted for the essay will result in immediate disqualification.

Applicants should therefore ensure that the essay represents their own authentic writing and personal experiences.

  1. Recommendation Form

Applicants must provide one letter of recommendation from their employer.

The recommendation should come from the applicant’s direct supervisor at their current job.

Applicants must use the official Recommendation Form and follow the instructions provided in the Application Booklet.

Because the recommendation requires involvement from a current supervisor, applicants should approach their supervisor sufficiently early to ensure that the document can be completed before the application deadline.

  1. English Proficiency Certificate

Applicants should attach a copy of any relevant certificate demonstrating English proficiency, if applicable.

Examples include:

  • TOEFL
  • TOEIC
  • Other recognised English-language proficiency certificates

Applicants should carefully review the official application instructions regarding acceptable documentation.

Important Rule Regarding AI-Generated Applications

One of the most important instructions for the IATSS Forum application concerns artificial intelligence.

The programme explicitly states that:

Submitting AI-generated text for the Basic Question Form or Essay will result in immediate disqualification.

This means applicants should not use AI-generated responses as their submitted answers for these components.

Applicants should instead write their responses themselves and ensure that their answers accurately communicate:

  • Their own experiences
  • Their own leadership journey
  • Their own challenges
  • Their own motivations
  • Their own understanding of issues
  • Their own goals
  • Their own reasons for applying

This requirement makes authenticity particularly important in preparing the application.

Applicants can carefully review the official instructions and application booklet, but their final responses for the Basic Question Form and Essay should be their own work.

Language Requirements for Application Documents

All submitted application documents must be written in English.

Applicants should also ensure that all documents are:

  • Complete
  • Clearly written
  • Legible
  • Properly formatted
  • Submitted in the required format

Handwritten forms will not be accepted.

Applicants should also be careful when using acronyms.

If an acronym is used, applicants must write out the full name the first time it appears.

For example:

International Association of Traffic and Safety Sciences (IATSS)

After introducing the full name, the acronym can then be used throughout the remainder of the document.

How to Apply for the IATSS Forum 2027

Applicants should follow the official application process carefully.

Step 1: Download the Application Materials

Applicants should download the official:

  • Application Booklet
  • Application Form
  • Basic Question Form
  • Essay Form
  • Recommendation Form
  • Other required application materials

The Application Booklet should be read carefully before completing the forms because it contains detailed instructions regarding the application requirements.

Step 2: Complete All Required Documents

Applicants should complete the required documents in English.

They should carefully review each form before submission to ensure that no required section has been left incomplete.

Applicants should also ensure that the information provided is consistent across all documents.

Step 3: Prepare the Documents for Online Submission

Applicants should convert their completed Word documents into PDF format before uploading them.

Scanned image files such as JPEG and PNG may also be accepted when they are clear and appropriately sized.

However, applicants are advised not to submit photographs of printed documents taken with a smartphone or camera.

The programme explains that such photographs may lose accuracy and readability when enlarged.

Applicants should therefore use properly scanned documents wherever possible.

Step 4: Rename the Files

Before uploading the documents, applicants must rename their files by adding their nickname to the beginning of the file name.

For example:

Abby_Application Form

This helps organize the submitted materials and should be completed before proceeding to the online application page.

Step 5: Sign in to a Google Account

Applicants need to sign in to a Google account to access the online application page.

Applicants who do not already have a Google account will need to create one.

The programme recommends using Google Chrome while signed in to the relevant Google account for optimal viewing.

Step 6: Upload the Documents Online

Once all required documents are prepared in PDF or acceptable image formats, applicants should upload them through the appropriate online application page corresponding to their nationality.

Applicants are advised to use a PC rather than a mobile device when submitting their application.

The application system allows progress to be automatically saved as a draft for 30 days from the applicant’s last edit.

If an applicant cannot complete the application in one sitting, they should make sure to sign in again using the same Google account to continue working on the application.

Step 7: Submit the Application

After uploading all required documents and completing the online application, applicants should review the submission carefully before finalizing it.

Applicants should avoid uploading multiple sets of the same documents.

The IATSS Forum specifically warns that submitting multiple sets may delay processing or result in an applicant missing an opportunity to be considered.

Postal Submission

The primary application process is online.

However, applicants who wish to submit their documents by post should contact their country secretariat in advance.

The relevant contact details are provided on the last page of the Application Booklet.

Applicants should therefore not send documents by post without first contacting the appropriate country secretariat.

Email Applications Are Not Accepted

Applicants should be aware that applications submitted by email are not accepted.

The required documents must be submitted through the official online application process unless an alternative submission arrangement has been discussed with the relevant country secretariat.

Important Application Instructions to Remember

Before submitting an application, candidates should carefully review the following requirements:

  1. The application deadline is 30 September 2026.
  2. Applications are accepted once a year.
  3. Applicants must be 35 years old or younger as of the application closing date.
  4. Applicants must currently be working full-time in a professional field, with self-employed and freelance professionals also eligible.
  5. Applicants should have at least two years of full-time professional experience.
  6. All documents must be written in English.
  7. Handwritten forms are not accepted.
  8. AI-generated text submitted for the Basic Question Form or Essay results in immediate disqualification.
  9. Applicants should provide one recommendation from their direct supervisor at their current job.
  10. English proficiency certificates should be provided if applicable.
  11. Applicants must carefully follow the instructions in the Application Booklet.
  12. Documents should be converted to PDF or prepared as acceptable, clear scanned images.
  13. Smartphone or camera photographs of printed documents should be avoided.
  14. Files should be renamed by adding the applicant’s nickname at the beginning.
  15. Applicants need a Google account to access the online application system.
  16. Google Chrome is recommended for accessing the online application page.
  17. Applicants are encouraged to use a PC rather than a mobile device.
  18. Application progress can be saved as a draft for 30 days from the last edit.
  19. Applicants must use the same Google account to resume a saved application.
  20. Multiple sets of application documents should not be uploaded.
  21. Applications by email are not accepted.
  22. Applicants wishing to submit documents by post should contact their country secretariat in advance.
  23. The programme period is subject to change.
  24. Applicants cannot guarantee which of the two 2027 programme periods they will be assigned to.

What Makes a Strong IATSS Forum Applicant?

A strong applicant is likely to be someone who can demonstrate a combination of professional experience, leadership, self-awareness, community awareness, collaborative ability, and a clear vision for future contribution.

Applicants should not simply focus on listing achievements.

Instead, they should demonstrate the connection between their experiences and their future goals.

For example, a compelling application should be able to explain:

What have I done?

This demonstrates professional and leadership experience.

What have I learned?

This demonstrates reflection and self-awareness.

What challenges does my community or country face?

This demonstrates awareness of issues.

What am I currently doing to address these challenges?

This demonstrates motivation and action.

What do I still need to learn?

This demonstrates openness to development.

Why is the IATSS Forum the right opportunity for me?

This demonstrates programme alignment.

How will I use the experience afterwards?

This demonstrates long-term potential and commitment to contributing to society.

Why Cross-Cultural Learning Matters in the IATSS Forum

One of the distinctive features of the IATSS Forum is its emphasis on learning across cultural and professional boundaries.

Participants will interact with people who may have very different experiences, professional expertise, social environments, and perspectives.

This creates an environment in which participants can challenge their existing assumptions, learn new approaches to leadership, and develop a broader understanding of regional issues.

The programme’s emphasis on collaborative leadership also means that participants are expected to contribute to the learning of others.

Every participant brings their own knowledge and experience, making the programme a two-way learning environment rather than a conventional classroom experience.

IATSS Forum and Future Leadership

The programme is particularly relevant for professionals who want to strengthen their ability to contribute to sustainable development and become more effective leaders in their communities and organizations.

The experience can provide an opportunity to develop greater awareness of:

  • Different leadership approaches
  • Regional challenges
  • Cross-cultural communication
  • Collaborative problem-solving
  • International cooperation
  • Professional networking
  • Personal strengths and areas for improvement
  • The role of diverse perspectives in creating solutions

Participants are expected to think beyond their immediate professional responsibilities and consider how their leadership can contribute to wider societal development.

Frequently Asked Questions About the IATSS Forum 2027

What is the IATSS Forum?

The IATSS Forum is an international leadership and learning programme designed to bring together professionals from participating Asian countries for cross-cultural exchange, leadership development, knowledge sharing, and engagement with regional and societal issues.

When is the IATSS Forum 2027?

There are two planned programme periods:

71st IATSS Forum: May to July 2027, lasting 8 weeks.

72nd IATSS Forum: September to November 2027, lasting 8 weeks.

The exact schedule may change.

Can applicants choose their programme period?

Applicants cannot guarantee which programme period they will be assigned to.

What is the application deadline?

The application period runs from 1 June 2026 to 30 September 2026.

The deadline is therefore 30 September 2026.

How much professional experience is required?

Applicants should have at least two years of full-time professional job experience at the time of application.

Can freelancers apply?

Yes. The eligibility information specifically states that self-employed and freelance applicants can apply, provided they meet the other requirements.

Do applicants need to be currently employed?

Applicants should currently be full-time employees working in a professional field. Self-employed and freelance professionals are also included in the eligibility requirements.

Is English proficiency required?

Yes. Applicants should have sufficient English skills to live and study abroad and actively participate in lectures, group discussions, and meetings.

Applicants can submit relevant English proficiency certificates such as TOEFL or TOEIC, if applicable.

Is an essay required?

Yes. Applicants must complete a short essay on the designated topic using the official form.

Can applicants use AI to write the essay?

No. The programme explicitly states that submitting AI-generated text for the Basic Question Form or Essay will result in immediate disqualification.

Is a recommendation letter required?

Yes. Applicants must submit one recommendation from their employer, specifically from their direct supervisor at their current job.

Can the application be submitted by email?

No. Email submissions are not accepted.

Can applicants submit their application by post?

Applicants who wish to submit documents by post should contact their country secretariat in advance.

Is a Google account required?

Yes. Applicants need to sign in to a Google account to access the online application page.

Can applicants apply using a mobile phone?

The programme recommends using a PC rather than a mobile device for the online application process.

How long can an unfinished online application be saved?

The online application system can automatically save progress as a draft for 30 days from the applicant’s last edit.

Applicants must use the same Google account to resume the application.

Final Checklist for IATSS Forum 2027 Applicants

Before submitting the application, applicants should make sure they have prepared:

  • Completed Application Form
  • Completed Basic Question Form
  • Completed Essay
  • Recommendation Form from their direct supervisor
  • English proficiency certificate, if applicable
  • All documents written in English
  • Documents converted to PDF or acceptable scanned formats
  • Clear and readable scans
  • Correctly renamed files with the applicant’s nickname
  • Google account for online submission
  • Access to a PC for the online application
  • Correct country-specific online application page
  • All required documents uploaded
  • Final application reviewed for completeness
  • Application submitted before 30 September 2026

Applicants should also ensure that they have not uploaded multiple sets of documents and have not submitted their application by email.

Conclusion

The IATSS Forum 2027 offers an opportunity for professionals from across participating Asian countries to develop their leadership capabilities through intensive international learning, cross-cultural exchange, collaboration, and knowledge sharing.

The programme is particularly suited to professionals who have already gained meaningful work experience and are now looking to strengthen their leadership potential, broaden their international perspective, understand different approaches to problem-solving, and contribute more effectively to sustainable development in their communities and countries.

The selection criteria go beyond professional experience. The IATSS Forum is looking for people who can demonstrate leadership, self-awareness, awareness of community and national challenges, collaborative ability, cultural adaptability, professional expertise, English communication skills, and a genuine desire to create positive change.

Applicants should therefore approach the application as an opportunity to demonstrate not only what they have achieved but also what they have learned, what challenges they want to address, what they still need to develop, and how they intend to use the experience for the benefit of others.

For those considering applying, preparation should begin well before the deadline. The application requires multiple documents, including a recommendation from a current direct supervisor, and applicants must carefully follow the instructions in the official Application Booklet.

Most importantly, applicants should remember that the IATSS Forum explicitly prohibits AI-generated text for the Basic Question Form and Essay. These sections should authentically represent the applicant’s own experiences, ideas, motivations, and aspirations.

With applications open from 1 June 2026 until 30 September 2026, eligible professionals who meet the requirements should carefully review the official application materials, prepare their documents, and submit their application through the designated online process before the deadline.

The IATSS Forum ultimately seeks individuals who can learn from diversity, collaborate across cultures, develop as leaders, and take what they gain from the experience back into their professional and wider communities to contribute to meaningful and sustainable change.

item.content:encoded:
The DPhil theme in Global Health: First Referral / District Hospital Service Provision in a Changing World offers an opportunity to undertake advanced research into how first-referral hospitals, district hospitals and higher-level hospitals can evolve to meet changing healthcare needs in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs).

The research theme focuses on one of the most important challenges facing health systems today: determining which healthcare services should be provided, where those services should be delivered, how they should be organised, and which health workers should provide them.

The theme is particularly relevant to countries experiencing financial constraints, changing disease patterns, rapid population growth, shortages of trained healthcare workers, technological transformation and reductions in international development funding. It also considers the implications of climate change and advances in artificial intelligence and other technologies for the future organisation and delivery of healthcare.

The DPhil research is associated with the Health Systems Collaborative (HSC) and a multidisciplinary team led by Professor Mike English. The team has extensive experience researching first-referral hospitals and is currently involved in the multi-country AFRHiCARE Partnership, which explores the role and function of first-referral hospitals in Kenya, Uganda and South Africa.

Applicants from low- and middle-income countries are particularly encouraged to apply, with potential opportunities for research collaboration involving institutions and experts in countries including Nepal, Vietnam, Burundi and the Democratic Republic of Congo, as well as experts based in the WHO Eastern Mediterranean Region.

Background to the DPhil Theme

Healthcare systems in many low- and middle-income countries are operating in an increasingly complex environment.

Countries must continue expanding and improving healthcare services while dealing with long-term fiscal constraints, geopolitical uncertainty and declining or changing international development funding. At the same time, health systems are being affected by climate change, rapid advances in technology and artificial intelligence, shortages of trained health workers and, particularly in Africa, rapidly growing populations.

These pressures create difficult decisions for governments, health planners, healthcare providers and other stakeholders.

One of the central questions is how health systems should determine the services that need to be provided at different levels of care.

For example, some services may be appropriately delivered within communities or primary healthcare facilities, while other services require the infrastructure, equipment, specialist skills and technical expertise available at first-referral or higher-level hospitals.

These decisions can have significant consequences for:

  • Healthcare equity
  • Quality of care
  • Health system efficiency
  • Patient outcomes
  • Health workforce planning
  • Hospital infrastructure
  • Medical technologies
  • Referral systems
  • Integration between different levels of healthcare
  • The organisation of primary and hospital-based services

The DPhil theme therefore takes a systems-wide approach, placing patients and communities at the centre of healthcare planning and recognising that effective healthcare often depends on strong integration between community services, primary care, first-referral hospitals and higher-level hospitals.

What Are First-Referral Hospitals?

First-referral hospitals, often referred to as district hospitals or general hospitals, occupy an important position within healthcare systems.

They provide services that may not be practical, affordable or efficient to deliver in smaller primary healthcare facilities but that are nevertheless essential to populations.

Examples of services that may be provided at first-referral hospitals include:

  • Emergency and trauma care
  • Comprehensive emergency obstetric care
  • Essential surgical services
  • Diagnostic imaging
  • Laboratory services
  • Acute neonatal care
  • Severe and complex childhood illness management
  • Acute and complex adult medical care
  • Potentially acute mental health services

However, first-referral hospitals should not be viewed as isolated facilities.

The research theme emphasises their role within Integrated Health Care Systems, where primary care, first-referral hospitals and higher-level hospitals have strategically planned and complementary responsibilities.

This means that decisions about hospital services must consider how different levels of the health system work together rather than examining individual facilities independently.

Focus of the DPhil Research

The DPhil theme examines how the roles of first-referral hospitals and higher-level hospitals are determined, planned and changed within integrated healthcare systems.

Research may examine these roles within:

  • National public health systems
  • Sub-national public health systems
  • Private not-for-profit healthcare systems
  • Private for-profit healthcare systems
  • Integrated primary healthcare systems
  • Primary care networks
  • Referral systems connecting different levels of healthcare

The research can therefore explore both policy-level decisions and the practical implications of those decisions for healthcare delivery.

A central concern is how health systems can make evidence-informed decisions about the services that should be provided at first-referral hospitals while ensuring that patients receive appropriate care at the right level.

Specific Aims of the Research

The DPhil theme has three closely interconnected areas of research.

1. Determining Which Services Should Be Provided at First-Referral Hospitals

The first area focuses on identifying the types of services that could or should be delivered at first-referral hospital level.

This involves examining changing healthcare needs and determining which services require the infrastructure, workforce, equipment and expertise available at these hospitals.

Research could explore how decisions about essential hospital services are influenced by:

  • Population needs
  • Disease patterns
  • Available healthcare infrastructure
  • Financial constraints
  • Workforce availability
  • Technological developments
  • Referral arrangements
  • Primary healthcare capacity
  • Higher-level hospital capacity

2. Developing the Future Health Workforce

The second area focuses on how the healthcare workforce should evolve to provide first-referral hospital care in the future.

Healthcare roles are increasingly being defined by specific skills and competencies rather than solely by traditional professional categories.

This creates opportunities to investigate:

  • Generalist and specialist roles
  • New health worker roles
  • Revised professional responsibilities
  • Task-shifting
  • Task-sharing
  • Workforce distribution
  • Workforce training
  • Skills and competencies required for first-referral hospitals

Research in this area can help policymakers understand how health workforce strategies should respond to changing service requirements, technological advances and financial constraints.

3. Leveraging New Technologies

The third area examines how healthcare systems can benefit from new technologies.

Advances in technology and artificial intelligence have the potential to change:

  • What healthcare services are provided
  • Where healthcare is delivered
  • Who provides healthcare
  • How healthcare workers make decisions
  • How health information is collected and analysed
  • How quality of care is monitored
  • How healthcare systems plan services

The research theme provides an opportunity to investigate how these technologies can be integrated responsibly and effectively within health systems in low- and middle-income settings.

Potential Research Questions

Applicants can develop research around a range of questions. The source identifies several examples that illustrate the scope of the DPhil theme.

1. How Are Technology and Artificial Intelligence Changing Healthcare Delivery?

One potential area of research is the impact of advances in technology and artificial intelligence on strategic healthcare planning and service delivery.

Research could investigate how technology may influence:

  • What healthcare services are provided
  • Where services are delivered
  • Who provides healthcare
  • How different levels of healthcare are connected
  • How community, primary care, first-referral hospitals and higher-level hospitals interact

This area is particularly important as artificial intelligence and digital technologies increasingly influence healthcare systems around the world.

2. How Can Health Information Systems Improve Quality and Service Planning?

Another major research area concerns health information systems.

Many low- and middle-income countries collect large amounts of routine health information, but health systems may not yet have sufficiently developed systems to use that information effectively for strategic planning, quality monitoring and service improvement.

Research could therefore examine how routine health information can be:

  • Collected effectively
  • Analysed appropriately
  • Used to monitor quality
  • Applied to service planning
  • Used to identify opportunities for improvement
  • Integrated into decision-making at hospital, sub-national and national levels

There have also been substantial efforts to define quality indicators for essential hospital services. Research may examine examples of good practice and investigate how they can inform improvements in other health systems.

3. How Should Health Workforce Strategies Address Changing Hospital Roles?

A further research question concerns the changing roles of healthcare workers within first-referral hospitals.

The growing emphasis on skills and competencies, combined with experimentation with task-shifting and task-sharing, raises important questions about the future organisation of hospital workforces.

Research could investigate how first-referral hospital workforces may need to change in response to:

  • Essential service requirements
  • New technologies
  • Artificial intelligence
  • Fiscal constraints
  • Changing disease burdens
  • Workforce shortages
  • New models of integrated healthcare

4. How Can First-Referral Hospitals Complement Integrated Primary Healthcare?

Another research area concerns the relationship between first-referral hospitals and integrated primary healthcare systems.

Research could examine how primary healthcare systems and primary care networks are being planned and implemented and determine what approaches are working in different geographical and health-system contexts.

The research can also consider the implications of the epidemiological transition and the increasing burden of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) for first-referral hospital services.

Research Approach and Methodology

DPhil students working within this theme are typically expected to have some skills in qualitative or quantitative data collection and analysis.

The specific research methods used will depend on the research question selected, the student’s interests and the needs of the project.

Students may develop skills in a range of approaches, including:

  • Policy reviews
  • Scoping reviews
  • Systematic reviews
  • Qualitative research
  • Realist reviews
  • Statistical analysis
  • Modelling
  • Formal mixed-methods research
  • Qualitative data collection and analysis
  • Quantitative data collection and analysis
  • Implementation science approaches

Students may also develop conceptual frameworks, Theory of Change models or Programme Theory as part of their research.

Specific studies may be designed to answer the research questions developed by individual DPhil students. Where required, students will prepare research proposals for ethical review.

Primary Research in Low- and Middle-Income Countries

Primary data collection in specifically identified low- and middle-income countries may be required depending on the research project and available funding.

However, the source notes that travel to low- and middle-income countries cannot be guaranteed.

This means that prospective students should consider the research requirements and funding circumstances associated with their specific project when developing their research plans.

New ethical approvals are also likely to be required for new research activities. These may take the form of amendments to existing ethical approvals or completely new, or de novo, applications.

Health Systems Collaborative and Research Environment

Successful DPhil students will join the multidisciplinary Health Systems Collaborative (HSC) research team.

The collaborative brings together expertise from areas including:

  • Clinical medicine
  • Epidemiology
  • Health services research
  • Implementation science
  • Social science
  • Systematic reviews
  • Health economics
  • Research methodology
  • Realist evaluation
  • Health policy and systems research

The research environment is international, with DPhil students and collaborators from multiple low- and middle-income countries.

Students can therefore become part of a research community that brings together different professional disciplines, methodological perspectives and geographical experiences.

Training Opportunities for DPhil Students

The DPhil theme also provides opportunities for students to strengthen their research and professional skills.

Students may have the opportunity to participate in classes associated with the MSc in Health Service Improvement and Evaluation (MSc HSIE).

Depending on their interests and circumstances, DPhil students may also contribute to the MSc programme as teaching assistants.

Beyond formal coursework, the Health Systems Collaborative holds regular internal learning and skills-building sessions covering the different methods used in health policy and systems research.

Students are also encouraged to participate in:

  • Online meetings with collaborators
  • Research workshops
  • Project-related learning activities
  • Methodological skills sessions
  • Research discussions
  • Training activities connected to the collaborative’s projects

These opportunities can help students develop a broader understanding of health systems research while strengthening the specific methodological skills needed for their individual DPhil projects.

International Research Collaboration

The research theme is strongly international in scope.

The Health Systems Collaborative is currently involved in research examining first-referral hospitals in:

  • Kenya
  • Uganda
  • South Africa

The team also identifies potential opportunities for developing work with collaborating institutions in:

  • Nepal
  • Vietnam
  • Burundi
  • Democratic Republic of Congo

There may also be opportunities to work with experts based in the WHO Eastern Mediterranean Region.

Applicants from these countries and other low- and middle-income countries are especially encouraged to apply.

Supervisors for the DPhil Theme

The DPhil theme is led by Professor Mike English, whose expertise includes health services research and implementation science.

Depending on the specific research question pursued, students may work with one or more additional supervisors.

Professor Mike English

Professor Mike English has expertise in:

  • Health services research
  • Implementation science

He is based within the University of Oxford’s Department of Tropical Medicine.

Dr Claire Blacklock

Dr Claire Blacklock brings expertise in:

  • Health services research
  • Health professions
  • Realist methodology

Dr Yingxi Zhao

Dr Yingxi Zhao has expertise in:

  • Health services research
  • Workforce research
  • Quantitative methods
  • Qualitative methods

Dr Claire Keene

Dr Claire Keene brings expertise in:

  • Longitudinal data analysis
  • Chronic disease care
  • Implementation science

Dr Vira Ameli

Dr Vira Ameli has expertise in:

  • Digital health
  • Health policy

The combination of these supervisory areas allows prospective students to develop research projects that draw on different methodological and substantive perspectives.

Relevant Research and Publications

The research theme is supported by a body of work examining health systems, first-referral hospitals, workforce organisation, quality improvement and healthcare delivery.

Examples identified in the source include research on the relational culture of healthcare workplaces and improvement interventions in neonatal care in Kenya, observational research examining neonatal nursing in high-mortality hospital settings in Kenya, and research on integrating physician assistants or associates into hospital teams.

Other work has examined the role of first-referral hospitals in low- and middle-income countries and their relationship with universal health coverage.

These publications provide useful background for understanding the broader research environment in which this DPhil theme is situated.

Why First-Referral Hospital Research Matters

First-referral hospitals can play a critical role in ensuring that patients receive services that cannot be efficiently provided at primary-care level.

However, their role needs to be carefully designed within the wider health system.

If first-referral hospitals are not appropriately integrated with primary healthcare and higher-level hospitals, patients may experience difficulties accessing appropriate care, while health systems may experience inefficiencies in the use of workforce, infrastructure and technology.

Research into first-referral hospitals can therefore contribute to broader health system goals, including:

  • Improving access to essential healthcare
  • Strengthening referral systems
  • Improving quality of care
  • Supporting more efficient health workforce planning
  • Strengthening hospital service delivery
  • Improving the use of health information
  • Supporting evidence-based health policy
  • Integrating new technologies into healthcare
  • Responding to changing disease patterns
  • Addressing the needs of growing populations

Who Should Consider This DPhil Theme?

This research theme may be particularly suitable for prospective doctoral researchers interested in global health, health systems, health services research, healthcare policy, hospital service delivery, implementation science, health workforce research, digital health, artificial intelligence in healthcare, primary healthcare integration and health systems improvement.

Applicants with interests in low- and middle-income country health systems may find the theme especially relevant.

The research environment is multidisciplinary, meaning that the theme can accommodate research questions drawing on different academic and methodological backgrounds, provided that the proposed research aligns with the overall focus of first-referral and higher-level hospital service provision within changing health systems.

Location and Academic Setting

The theme is associated with the NDM Centre for Global Health Research.

The supervisory and research environment is connected to the University of Oxford’s work in global health, health services research and health systems research.

The DPhil theme reference number is 1718.

Application and Admissions Information

Prospective applicants should refer to the relevant University of Oxford admissions information and the specific requirements associated with the DPhil programme when preparing an application.

The research theme is intended to provide a framework for developing a doctoral research project rather than prescribing a single research question for every student.

Applicants should therefore consider how their proposed research interests align with the theme’s focus on:

  1. First-referral and district hospital service provision.
  2. Integrated healthcare systems.
  3. Health workforce development.
  4. Health information systems.
  5. Technology and artificial intelligence.
  6. Primary healthcare and referral networks.
  7. Quality improvement.
  8. Health policy and systems research.
  9. The changing burden of disease.
  10. Healthcare delivery in low- and middle-income countries.

APPLY HERE

Deadline

The deadline for applications to be considered for internal funding for entry in 2027 is Tuesday 1st December 2026. We recommend that you submit your application well in advance of the deadline – two or three weeks earlier.

There are three routes via which you can apply:

  • Via an advertised DPhil theme
  • By submitting your own project proposal as agreed with a supervisor
  • Via an allied funded programme

Visit HERE to learn more about the DPhil in Global Health.

Conclusion

The DPhil in Global Health: First Referral / District Hospital Service Provision in a Changing World provides a research-focused opportunity to investigate how health systems can adapt first-referral and higher-level hospitals to changing healthcare needs.

The theme recognises that healthcare delivery is being reshaped by financial pressures, workforce shortages, demographic changes, climate change, evolving disease patterns, technological advances and artificial intelligence. Against this background, it seeks research that can help policymakers and health systems determine which services should be delivered, where they should be delivered and how healthcare workers and technologies can be organised to provide high-quality care.

With access to the multidisciplinary Health Systems Collaborative, opportunities to engage with health policy and systems research methods, and potential connections to research programmes across several low- and middle-income countries, the theme offers a strong environment for doctoral research focused on practical health system challenges.

The research can contribute to important questions about the future of district and first-referral hospitals, including how they can complement primary healthcare, strengthen referral systems, use health information more effectively, develop appropriate workforces and take advantage of new technologies while keeping patients and communities at the centre of healthcare planning.

For prospective researchers interested in improving healthcare delivery in low- and middle-income countries, this DPhil theme offers an opportunity to undertake rigorous doctoral research on issues with significant implications for health policy, healthcare quality and health system performance.

Source: University of Oxford DPhil theme information, Global Health: First Referral / District Hospital Service Provision in a Changing World, theme reference 1718.
