item.content:encoded:
The King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) offers fully funded graduate study opportunities for students seeking advanced education and research experience in science, engineering, technology and related interdisciplinary fields.

Located in Thuwal, Saudi Arabia, KAUST is a graduate research university focused on science and technology. Its graduate admissions system provides opportunities to pursue Master’s and PhD degrees while admitted students receive the KAUST Fellowship, which provides comprehensive financial support for the duration of their graduate studies.

KAUST’s academic portfolio covers areas ranging from environmental science, marine science and plant science to bioscience, bioengineering, computer science, applied mathematics, electrical and computer engineering, statistics, chemical engineering, chemistry, earth system science, materials science, physics and mechanical engineering. The university also offers a Technology Innovation and Entrepreneurship Master’s programme.

For students interested in pursuing graduate-level research in science, engineering, technology and related fields, KAUST provides an opportunity to combine advanced coursework with research in an internationally oriented graduate environment.

About King Abdullah University of Science and Technology

The King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) is a graduate research university in Saudi Arabia. The university describes itself as a research-focused institution of science and technology, with a strong emphasis on interdisciplinary research and innovation.

KAUST’s academic structure brings together several major research divisions, including:

  • Biological and Environmental Science and Engineering
  • Biomedical Sciences
  • Computer, Electrical and Mathematical Science and Engineering
  • Physical Science and Engineering

The university also supports research centres and platforms in areas such as generative artificial intelligence, renewable energy and storage technologies, smart health and sustainable food security.

This research orientation makes KAUST particularly relevant to applicants interested in careers and further academic development in STEM and research-intensive disciplines.

KAUST Graduate Degree Programs

KAUST offers graduate-level programmes leading to Master’s and PhD degrees. The university’s official study information lists the following major programmes.

Technology Innovation and Entrepreneurship

KAUST offers a Technology Innovation and Entrepreneurship Master’s programme, designed for students interested in the intersection of technology, innovation and entrepreneurship.

This pathway can be particularly relevant to applicants who want to understand how scientific and technological research can be translated into innovation, products, services and wider economic or societal impact.

Biological and Environmental Science and Engineering

The Biological and Environmental Science and Engineering area includes:

  • Environmental Science and Engineering
  • Marine Science
  • Plant Science

These programmes are relevant to students interested in environmental systems, marine ecosystems, sustainability, natural resources, climate-related research, biological systems and related areas.

Biomedical Sciences

The Biomedical Sciences division includes:

  • Bioscience
  • Bioengineering

These programmes provide graduate-level opportunities for students interested in biological research, biomedical technologies, engineering approaches to health and related scientific disciplines.

Computer, Electrical and Mathematical Science and Engineering

KAUST offers several programmes within this area, including:

  • Applied Mathematics and Computational Science
  • Computer Science
  • Electrical and Computer Engineering
  • Statistics

These programmes provide opportunities for students interested in computational research, mathematics, artificial intelligence, data, statistics, computing, electronics, electrical systems and related technologies.

Physical Science and Engineering

The Physical Science and Engineering division includes:

  • Chemical Engineering
  • Chemistry
  • Earth System Science and Engineering
  • Materials Science and Engineering and Applied Physics
  • Mechanical Engineering

These programmes cover a broad range of scientific and engineering disciplines and can support research in areas such as materials, energy, chemical processes, earth systems, applied physics and mechanical systems.

Fully Funded KAUST Fellowship

One of the major features of KAUST graduate admissions is the KAUST Fellowship.

According to the university’s admissions information, all admitted students receive the KAUST Fellowship, which supports students for the duration of their graduate studies.

The fellowship includes several forms of financial support.

1. Full Tuition Support

The KAUST Fellowship provides full tuition support for admitted graduate students.

This is significant for students who might otherwise face substantial tuition costs associated with graduate education.

2. Annual Living Allowance

The fellowship includes a monthly living allowance equivalent to approximately US$20,000–30,000 per year, depending on the student’s qualifications and progression through the degree programme.

The exact amount is therefore not necessarily identical for every student.

3. Housing

KAUST provides housing as part of the fellowship package.

The university notes that charges may apply in certain circumstances, particularly in relation to dependent housing. Applicants with families should therefore review the specific housing provisions applicable to their situation.

4. Medical and Dental Coverage

The KAUST Fellowship also includes medical and dental coverage.

As with housing, the university notes that charges may apply to dependent coverage, meaning students should distinguish between the coverage provided to the student and arrangements for accompanying dependants.

5. Relocation Support

Admitted students also receive relocation support, helping them transition to KAUST in Saudi Arabia.

Taken together, these provisions make the KAUST Fellowship a comprehensive graduate funding package rather than simply a tuition scholarship.

KAUST Master’s and PhD Admissions

KAUST’s graduate admissions process begins with selecting an appropriate academic programme.

Applicants are encouraged to explore the available programmes, research areas and faculty profiles before beginning their application. The university’s application process is designed to help prospective students identify a programme that matches their academic background, research interests and career objectives.

The basic application process involves five major stages:

  1. Find a programme.
  2. Review the admissions timeline.
  3. Check the required documentation.
  4. Create an application account and complete the application.
  5. Submit the completed application.

This means applicants should not wait until the final days before the deadline to begin preparing their application.

Step 1: Find a Suitable KAUST Programme

The first step is identifying the graduate programme that best matches the applicant’s academic and research interests.

Prospective students should review:

  • Available Master’s programmes
  • PhD programmes
  • Faculty profiles
  • Research groups
  • Research areas
  • Academic requirements
  • Programme-specific information

KAUST encourages applicants to explore faculty and research areas before applying. This is particularly important for research-oriented graduate study because the alignment between an applicant’s interests and the university’s research environment can be an important part of preparing a strong application.

Step 2: Check the Admissions Timeline

Applicants should carefully review the official KAUST admissions timeline because application deadlines differ according to the intended entry period and degree programme.

For the current Fall 2027 admission cycle, KAUST lists the following dates:

  • Application opens: 28 September 2026
  • Application deadline: 3 January 2027
  • Admission decisions: 14 February 2027
  • Fall semester begins: 29 August 2027

Fall 2027 admission is open to MS, MS/PhD and PhD applicants.

KAUST also has a Spring 2027 admission cycle, but the current timeline states that Spring 2027 admission is open only to PhD applicants. The Round 1 deadline was 27 September 2026, with decisions scheduled for 8 November 2026 and the spring semester beginning on 17 January 2027.

Therefore, applicants seeking a Master’s opportunity should pay particular attention to the Fall 2027 cycle.

KAUST Application Deadline for Fall 2027

The current official admissions timeline lists:

Fall 2027 application deadline: 3 January 2027.

KAUST notes that the dates are tentative and may change depending on application volume. Applicants should therefore check the official admissions timeline regularly and avoid relying solely on previously published dates.

Step 3: Prepare the Required Documents

KAUST requires applicants to provide a range of supporting documentation.

The admissions information identifies the following major requirements:

  • Official university transcripts or academic records
  • Graduation certificate where applicable
  • Certified English translations for documents issued in another language
  • English-language test results where required
  • Three letters of recommendation
  • Curriculum vitae

Applicants should begin collecting these documents early because some, particularly recommendation letters and official academic records, may take time to obtain.

Academic Transcripts

Applicants must submit an official and complete academic record from every institution previously attended.

The transcript should be uploaded in the original language together with a certified English translation where the original document is not in English.

KAUST also requires the university grading scale to be included with the submitted academic documentation.

Applicants who receive an offer will subsequently need to provide the official final transcript to the KAUST Office of Admissions before arrival as part of the onboarding process.

English Language Requirements

English proficiency is an important component of the KAUST graduate admissions process.

The university requires a minimum:

  • TOEFL iBT score of 81, or
  • IELTS score of 6.5.

Only official TOEFL or IELTS scores are accepted under the stated requirements. KAUST’s admissions code for TOEFL is 4107.

Who Is Exempt from the TOEFL or IELTS Requirement?

A TOEFL or IELTS score is not required if the applicant obtained a degree from an accredited institution in one of the following countries:

  • United States
  • Canada
  • United Kingdom
  • Ireland
  • Australia
  • New Zealand

Applicants who do not fall under these exemptions should carefully plan for an accepted English-language test before the application deadline.

Is the GRE Required?

KAUST does not require the GRE for admission.

However, the university states that it strongly encourages applicants to take the GRE General Test. A strong quantitative score can enhance an application, particularly for students applying to quantitatively intensive science, technology, engineering and mathematics programmes.

Official GRE results should be sent directly from ETS using KAUST’s admissions code 4139.

Therefore, while the GRE is not a compulsory admission requirement, applicants who have the opportunity to take it may consider submitting a strong result as an additional component of their application.

Three Letters of Recommendation

Applicants must have three recommendation letters submitted on their behalf.

KAUST indicates that these recommendations are important and should ideally come from professors or academic advisers who have taught the applicant in their major field or supervised their research.

Strong recommendations should provide more than general statements about an applicant’s character.

The university recommends that recommenders discuss:

  • How they know the applicant
  • The applicant’s academic or research performance
  • Research ability
  • Comparative performance, such as being among the strongest students in a class or cohort
  • Relevant academic strengths

Recommendations are submitted directly through the application by the recommenders.

Applicants should therefore approach potential recommenders well in advance of the application deadline.

Curriculum Vitae

Applicants must also provide a Curriculum Vitae (CV).

A strong graduate-school CV should clearly present relevant:

  • Academic qualifications
  • Research experience
  • Publications, where applicable
  • Research projects
  • Technical skills
  • Laboratory experience
  • Internships
  • Professional experience
  • Academic awards
  • Conferences and presentations
  • Leadership or relevant extracurricular activities

The most important consideration is relevance. Applicants should ensure that their CV demonstrates their preparation for the specific graduate programme they are applying to.

Creating a KAUST Application Account

After identifying a programme and preparing the necessary documentation, applicants need to create an application account.

The application process allows applicants to upload their supporting documents as they become available.

This is useful for applicants who are still waiting for certain documents, such as recommendation letters or official academic records, because they can return to the application account and continue completing the required sections.

However, applicants should not interpret the ability to upload documents progressively as a reason to postpone preparation. It is better to begin early and leave sufficient time for reviewing the final application.

Submitting the KAUST Application

Once all required supporting documentation has been uploaded, applicants must log into their account and submit the application.

The university’s application guidance emphasises the importance of completing the supporting documentation before submission.

Applicants should carefully review the application before final submission to ensure:

  • Personal information is correct.
  • The intended programme is correct.
  • Academic records are complete.
  • English-language documentation is included where required.
  • Recommendation requests have been submitted.
  • The CV is uploaded.
  • Required supporting documents are properly uploaded.
  • Information across different sections is consistent.

KAUST Research Environment

KAUST is strongly research-oriented, making the university particularly relevant to students who want to pursue research-intensive graduate careers.

The university’s research portfolio includes areas such as:

  • Generative artificial intelligence
  • Renewable energy
  • Energy storage
  • Smart health
  • Sustainable food security
  • Environmental science
  • Marine science
  • Plant science
  • Bioscience
  • Bioengineering
  • Computer science
  • Applied mathematics
  • Electrical and computer engineering
  • Statistics
  • Chemistry
  • Chemical engineering
  • Earth system science
  • Materials science
  • Applied physics
  • Mechanical engineering

KAUST also provides access to major research infrastructure, including research platforms, core laboratories and the Shaheen III supercomputer.

This research ecosystem can be particularly relevant to graduate applicants who intend to pursue research, innovation or technology-driven careers.

Learn More HERE

Who Should Consider Applying?

KAUST is particularly relevant to students with academic backgrounds and research interests connected to science, engineering, technology, mathematics, computing, environmental sciences and related disciplines.

Potential applicants include graduates interested in:

  • Computer science
  • Artificial intelligence and computational research
  • Mathematics
  • Statistics
  • Electrical and computer engineering
  • Chemical engineering
  • Chemistry
  • Mechanical engineering
  • Materials science
  • Applied physics
  • Earth and environmental sciences
  • Marine science
  • Plant science
  • Bioscience
  • Bioengineering
  • Technology innovation and entrepreneurship

However, applicants should always confirm the specific requirements of their chosen programme rather than assuming that a general academic background automatically qualifies them.

International Applicants and Geographic Eligibility

KAUST’s graduate admissions process is internationally oriented, and the university describes its community as bringing together global perspectives to address scientific challenges.

The admissions information provided does not specify a nationality or racial restriction for the general Master’s and PhD admissions process. Therefore, applicants should assess eligibility primarily against the academic, programme-specific, language and documentation requirements.

The opportunity should not, however, be described as restricted to a particular race, ethnicity or continent based on the information provided.

Applicants from Africa, Asia, Europe, the Americas, the Middle East and other regions should consult the official KAUST admissions requirements and the specific programme information applicable to them.

Why the KAUST Fellowship Is Important

Graduate education abroad can involve significant expenses, including tuition, accommodation, healthcare, living expenses and relocation.

The KAUST Fellowship addresses several of these major cost categories.

For admitted students, the package includes:

  1. Full tuition support.
  2. Annual living support of approximately US$20,000–30,000 depending on qualifications and degree progression.
  3. Housing.
  4. Medical coverage.
  5. Dental coverage.
  6. Relocation support.

The combination of these benefits means that successful applicants can focus substantially on their graduate studies and research rather than having to independently finance the major costs associated with studying abroad.

Important Things Applicants Should Do Before Applying

Prospective KAUST applicants should begin preparing well before the deadline.

1. Identify the right programme

Do not choose a programme simply because it is fully funded. Examine the curriculum, research areas, faculty members and academic requirements to determine whether the programme fits your goals.

2. Research faculty members

Graduate study at a research-intensive university requires serious attention to research alignment.

Applicants should explore faculty profiles and identify researchers whose work connects with their interests.

3. Prepare for English testing

If you are not exempt from the English-language requirement, plan for the TOEFL or IELTS early.

Waiting until close to the application deadline can create unnecessary pressure.

4. Contact recommenders early

Three recommendations are required, and recommenders need sufficient time to prepare thoughtful letters.

Approach professors, academic supervisors or research advisers early rather than requesting recommendations immediately before the deadline.

5. Organise academic records

Collect transcripts from every institution attended and ensure that documents not issued in English have the required certified English translations.

6. Build a research-focused CV

Your CV should communicate your preparation for graduate study and research.

Highlight academic projects, research experience, publications, technical skills, internships and other achievements that are relevant to the programme.

7. Consider taking the GRE

Although the GRE is not required, KAUST states that it strongly encourages applicants to take the GRE General Test and notes that a high quantitative score can strengthen an application.

Learn More HERE

KAUST Admissions 2027: Key Dates

For applicants targeting Fall 2027 entry, the current official timeline provides the following schedule:

Admission Stage Date
Fall 2027 applications open 28 September 2026
Fall 2027 application deadline 3 January 2027
Admission decisions released 14 February 2027
Fall 2027 semester begins 29 August 2027

These dates are identified by KAUST as tentative and may change depending on application volume.

For Spring 2027, the current timeline indicates that admission is open only to PhD applicants. The Round 1 deadline was 27 September 2026.

Applicants should therefore use the official KAUST admissions timeline as the final reference before submitting an application.

KAUST Scholarship 2027: Key Details

University: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST)

Location: Thuwal, Saudi Arabia

Study level: Master’s and PhD

Main areas: Science, engineering, technology, mathematics, computing, environmental sciences, biomedical sciences and related fields

Funding: KAUST Fellowship

Tuition: Fully supported

Living allowance: Approximately US$20,000–30,000 annually, depending on qualifications and progression

Housing: Provided

Medical and dental coverage: Provided, with conditions concerning dependants

Relocation: Supported

English requirement: TOEFL iBT 81 or IELTS 6.5, subject to stated exemptions

GRE: Not required, but strongly encouraged

Recommendations: Three

CV: Required

Fall 2027 application deadline: 3 January 2027

Fall 2027 semester: Begins 29 August 2027

How to Apply

Applicants should begin through the official KAUST admissions website and follow the university’s application process.

The process can be summarised as follows:

  1. Explore KAUST’s Master’s and PhD programmes.
  2. Review relevant faculty members and research areas.
  3. Check the applicable admissions timeline.
  4. Review the entry and documentation requirements.
  5. Prepare transcripts, English-language results, recommendation letters and CV.
  6. Create an online application account.
  7. Upload the required documents.
  8. Review the completed application carefully.
  9. Submit the application before the applicable deadline.

Applicants should use the official admissions website for the latest application instructions and programme-specific requirements.

Visit HERE and HERE to learn more and apply for the KAUST Scholarship 2027.

Conclusion

The KAUST Scholarship 2027 provides an important opportunity for students seeking fully funded graduate education in science, engineering and technology. Through the KAUST Fellowship, admitted students receive full tuition support, a substantial annual living allowance, housing, medical and dental coverage and relocation support.

The university offers a broad portfolio of Master’s and PhD programmes spanning environmental science, marine science, plant science, bioscience, bioengineering, computer science, applied mathematics, statistics, electrical and computer engineering, chemistry, chemical engineering, earth system science, materials science, applied physics and mechanical engineering.

For students targeting Fall 2027 entry, the current application deadline is 3 January 2027, while the semester is scheduled to begin on 29 August 2027. Because KAUST notes that admissions dates are tentative and may change, prospective applicants should regularly check the official admissions timeline.

The strongest applicants should begin preparing early by identifying an appropriate programme, researching faculty and research areas, arranging three strong academic recommendations, preparing their CV and transcripts, and meeting the required English-language standards.

For anyone seeking a research-intensive graduate education with comprehensive financial support, KAUST represents an opportunity worth carefully investigating, provided the applicant meets the requirements of the specific programme.

Applications are now open for EMMIR Edition 14 (2027–2029), the European Master in Migration and Intercultural Relations, an international two-year Erasmus Mundus Joint Master’s programme focused on migration, intercultural relations and the social, cultural and political dimensions of human mobility.

The programme brings together an international consortium of higher education institutions across Europe, Africa and Asia, giving students the opportunity to study migration and intercultural relations through a multidisciplinary and international academic environment.

For the 2027–2029 intake, applications for Erasmus+ scholarships and non-fee-paying study places are open until 20 December 2026. Applicants seeking fee-paying self-funded study places may apply until the available places are assigned or, at the latest, 15 July 2027, subject to availability.

The EMMIR programme is designed for graduates who want to develop advanced academic and professional expertise in migration studies, intercultural relations and related areas. It combines classroom learning, international mobility, research, practical experience and an internship component across different stages of the programme.

What Is EMMIR?

EMMIR stands for the European Master in Migration and Intercultural Relations.

It is a two-year, four-semester Master’s programme that examines migration and intercultural relations from interdisciplinary and intercultural perspectives.

Rather than limiting students to one university or one national academic environment, EMMIR incorporates international mobility as a central part of the programme.

Students begin their studies together at the University of Oldenburg in Germany and continue the second semester at the University of Stavanger in Norway. During the third semester, students select an individual mobility path that includes a focus module and a project-based internship at one of the EMMIR partner institutions. The fourth semester focuses primarily on thesis research and writing.

This structure enables students to experience different academic environments and to examine migration and intercultural relations from multiple geographical and disciplinary perspectives.

EMMIR Edition 14: 2027–2029

The current application cycle is for EMMIR Edition 14, which will run from 2027 to 2029.

According to the current EMMIR programme timeline, applications opened on 1 October 2026.

The programme is scheduled to begin with orientation and an intensive phase on 1 September 2027. The first semester will take place at the University of Oldenburg, followed by the second semester at the University of Stavanger.

The programme timeline includes:

  • Applications open: 1 October 2026
  • Scholarship and non-fee-paying application deadline: 20 December 2026
  • Admissions notifications: Beginning/mid-April 2027
  • Programme orientation: 1 September 2027
  • Intensive phase: September 2027
  • Semester 1: October–December 2027, University of Oldenburg
  • Semester 2: January–May/June 2028, University of Stavanger
  • Semester 3: June/July–November 2028, including a project-based internship
  • Semester 4: December 2028–June 2029, focusing on the Master’s thesis
  • Thesis submission: 30 June 2029
  • Graduation: September 2029

Application Deadlines for EMMIR Edition 14

There are different deadlines depending on the type of application.

Erasmus+ Scholarship and Non-Fee-Paying Study Places

The deadline for applicants seeking an Erasmus+ scholarship or a non-fee-paying study place is:

20 December 2026 at 23:59 CET (Germany time).

Applicants interested in an Erasmus+ scholarship must apply within this deadline.

Fee-Paying Self-Funded Study Places

Applicants who intend to study as fee-paying self-funded students can apply on a first-come, first-served basis until the available study places are assigned.

The latest possible application deadline is:

15 July 2027

This route therefore remains open longer than the scholarship and non-fee-paying routes, but applicants should understand that availability is not guaranteed until that date.

Visit HERE for more information about EMMIR Erasmus Mundus Joint Master’s 2027–2029.

Erasmus+ Scholarship Opportunity

One of the most attractive aspects of EMMIR is the opportunity to apply for a limited number of Erasmus+ scholarships.

Scholarship applicants are selected based on merit.

According to the current EMMIR funding information, Erasmus+ scholarship holders receive:

  • €1,400 per month for 24 months
  • Coverage of health insurance
  • Coverage of university registration fees
  • Coverage of student service fees

The scholarship therefore provides substantial financial support throughout the two-year Master’s programme.

However, scholarship applicants should carefully understand what the funding does and does not cover.

The scholarship holders are expected to use their monthly scholarship to cover mobility-related costs such as:

  • Travel
  • Visa expenses
  • Vaccinations
  • Residence permit fees
  • Other required mobility expenses

The current EMMIR funding information states that there are no separate additional payments for travel and installation.

Non-Fee-Paying Study Places

EMMIR also provides opportunities for students who are not awarded an Erasmus+ scholarship but are selected for a non-fee-paying self-funded place.

Students in this category do not have to pay the programme participation costs.

Their health insurance, university registration and student service fees are also covered.

However, they remain responsible for their living expenses and travel costs associated with the programme’s required mobility path. They must also demonstrate that they have sufficient financial resources to cover their living costs for the two-year programme when applying for a student visa, where applicable.

Fee-Paying Self-Funded Option

Students who are not applying for or do not receive scholarship or non-fee-paying funding may apply as fee-paying self-funded students.

The current participation cost is listed as:

€4,500 per semester.

The participation costs cover obligatory programme activities, health insurance, registration and student service fees at the relevant hosting university.

They do not cover accommodation, food, general living expenses or travel.

Fee-paying students must therefore plan carefully for the total cost of completing the two-year programme, particularly because EMMIR includes international mobility between different locations.

What Does the EMMIR Programme Study?

EMMIR focuses on Migration and Intercultural Relations, making it particularly relevant to students interested in the movement of people, migration policies, cultural diversity, integration, intercultural communication and related social issues.

The programme takes an interdisciplinary approach rather than examining migration from only one academic perspective.

Potentially relevant academic areas include:

  • Migration studies
  • Intercultural relations
  • Social sciences
  • History
  • Cultural studies
  • Educational sciences
  • Law
  • Economics
  • Development studies
  • Journalism
  • Empirical social research
  • International and intercultural studies

Applicants are expected to demonstrate prior knowledge relevant to migration studies, intercultural relations and empirical research methods.

International and Multidisciplinary Learning

One of the defining features of EMMIR is its international academic structure.

Students experience different academic and cultural environments during the programme, beginning in Germany and Norway before undertaking an individual mobility path in the third semester.

The third semester includes a project-based internship and a focus module at one of the partner institutions.

This provides students with an opportunity to connect academic knowledge with practical experience in migration and intercultural relations.

The final semester is dedicated to developing and completing the Master’s thesis, with students able to shape their mobility and research arrangements around their chosen thesis topic.

EMMIR’s Four-Semester Structure

Semester 1: University of Oldenburg, Germany

The first semester takes place at the University of Oldenburg.

Students study together as a cohort and begin developing a common academic foundation in migration and intercultural relations.

The semester follows an intensive academic structure, with the programme’s first semester beginning in October 2027 after the September orientation and intensive phase.

Semester 2: University of Stavanger, Norway

The second semester takes place at the University of Stavanger.

This continues the shared academic component of the programme while exposing students to another national and academic context.

Semester 3: Individual Mobility and Internship

The third semester provides greater individualisation.

Students select a mobility path that includes:

  • A focus module
  • A project-based internship
  • Study at one of the EMMIR partner institutions

The internship component allows students to connect their academic preparation with practical experience.

Semester 4: Master’s Thesis

The fourth semester is primarily dedicated to thesis research and writing.

Students participate in a proposal colloquium and then develop their Master’s thesis under academic supervision.

The thesis is scheduled for submission by 30 June 2029 for Edition 14.

Who Should Apply?

EMMIR is particularly suitable for graduates who have an academic or professional interest in migration, intercultural relations and related social and policy issues.

Applicants should normally have a first university degree such as a Bachelor’s degree or equivalent qualification in a relevant discipline.

The official entry requirements identify fields including:

  • Social sciences
  • History
  • Cultural studies
  • Educational sciences
  • Law
  • Economics
  • Development studies
  • Journalism

Applicants from related fields may also be considered where their academic background demonstrates relevance to the programme.

Academic Requirements

Applicants are expected to meet the academic entry requirements for EMMIR.

The programme normally requires a first degree equivalent to a Bachelor’s degree in an area related to migration studies.

The final grade of the first degree should be at least equivalent to C+, with supporting documentation required.

Applicants should also demonstrate academic knowledge of:

  • Migration studies
  • Intercultural relations
  • Empirical methods

This knowledge can be demonstrated through relevant undergraduate modules, papers, essays, examination results and other appropriate academic documentation.

Relevant professional experience can also strengthen an application, as the EMMIR selection process gives preference to qualified applicants who have relevant professional experience.

Age of Previous Degree

The official EMMIR entry requirements state that the applicant’s last degree should generally not be older than five years.

Applicants whose degree is older than five years should explain in their statement of purpose why they have decided to return to university.

This requirement makes it particularly important for applicants with older academic qualifications to clearly explain their current motivation and connection to the field.

Can Applicants Who Already Have a Master’s Degree Apply?

Yes, applicants who already hold a Master’s degree may still apply.

However, because EMMIR itself leads to a Master’s degree, applicants who already have a Master’s qualification are expected to convincingly explain why they want to pursue another Master’s degree.

The explanation should make clear how EMMIR fits into the applicant’s academic, professional or research trajectory.

English Language Requirements

Applicants must demonstrate English-language proficiency if English is not their native language or if their undergraduate education was not conducted in English.

EMMIR accepts different forms of evidence depending on the applicant’s circumstances.

Possible evidence can include:

  • Recognised English-language competency tests
  • Proof that higher education was completed in English
  • Proof of professional work in an English-language environment
  • Other accepted documentation of English proficiency

The programme may contact applicants at a later stage to verify their language skills.

English Language Waivers

Certain applicants may request an English-language proficiency waiver.

The official requirements identify circumstances including applicants who:

  • Come from countries where English is one of several official languages
  • Obtained an undergraduate degree from Australia, Canada, Ireland, the United Kingdom, the United States or New Zealand
  • Spent at least two consecutive academic years studying at a higher education institution in one of those countries within the previous five years, with English as the language of instruction
  • Have at least two years of professional experience in an international company where English is the official working language
  • Can provide documented evidence that their higher education was completed in English or that they worked professionally in an English-language setting

The EMMIR Consortium Committee retains the right to request evidence of English proficiency even where an applicant requests a waiver.

Additional Language Requirement for Native English Speakers

Applicants whose native language is English are also subject to a language requirement.

They must demonstrate proficiency in a second language relevant to migration studies by the application deadline at the required level.

Applicants may be asked to justify why their chosen second language is relevant to migration studies.

This reflects the intercultural and international nature of the EMMIR programme.

Selection Criteria

EMMIR receives a large number of applications, making preparation important.

The Consortium Committee Selection Board considers several factors when evaluating applications, including:

  1. Relevance and level of academic qualifications
  2. Relevance and level of research or professional experience
  3. Motivation
  4. Proficiency in a second or third language

These criteria mean that applicants should not rely solely on academic grades. A strong application should demonstrate why the applicant is academically and professionally suited to migration and intercultural studies and why EMMIR is the right programme for their goals.

How to Apply for EMMIR Edition 14

Applications are submitted online through the eMundus application platform.

The application process involves several stages.

Step 1: Register on eMundus

Applicants first register on the EMMIR online application management platform using their name and email address.

After registration, applicants can access the online application form.

Step 2: Complete the Online Application

The application form must be completed in English.

Applicants can complete the form section by section and return to continue their application later, with information saved to the system.

Applicants are expected to provide complete and accurate information.

Step 3: Upload Supporting Documents

The online application requires relevant supporting documentation.

Key documents include:

  • Valid passport
  • Curriculum vitae
  • Statement of Purpose
  • First university degree diploma and transcript
  • Other relevant academic qualifications
  • English-language proficiency documentation
  • Other relevant supporting documents

Documents should be submitted in English or accompanied by an official English translation where necessary.

Step 4: Submit Before the Deadline

Applicants for Erasmus+ scholarships and non-fee-paying study places must submit the completed application by:

20 December 2026 at 23:59 CET.

Applicants should not wait until the final hours because incomplete applications or documents that fail to meet the programme’s requirements can result in the withdrawal or exclusion of an application.

APPLY HERE

Statement of Purpose

The Statement of Purpose is an important part of the application.

Applicants are expected to explain their motivation for studying EMMIR and demonstrate why the programme fits their academic and professional goals.

A strong statement should establish a clear connection between:

  • The applicant’s academic background
  • Previous research or professional experience
  • Interest in migration and intercultural relations
  • Motivation for joining EMMIR
  • Future academic or professional objectives

The official application procedures specify a one- to two-page Statement of Purpose.

Application Documents and Verification

The online application forms the basis for the initial admission decision.

Applicants whose applications are successful will subsequently be asked to submit certified hard copies of their documents.

Successful applicants generally have 10 calendar days after receiving their notification letter to send the required certified documents and provide proof of dispatch.

The EMMIR team then verifies the documents before issuing the final admission documentation.

Applicants should therefore ensure that all information entered online matches the supporting documents they submit.

Discrepancies or irregularities in the documentation can affect admission.

Important Information About the EMMIR Scholarship

Applicants should understand that applying for EMMIR does not automatically mean receiving an Erasmus+ scholarship.

The programme has a very limited number of Erasmus+ scholarships, and scholarship holders are selected based on merit.

Applicants indicate their preferred funding option during the application process. The choice of funding option does not need to be justified and does not affect how the application is rated.

Applicants who have previously benefited from an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master scholarship are not eligible to receive an additional Erasmus Mundus scholarship.

EMMIR and International Mobility

International mobility is one of the central features of EMMIR.

Students do not simply study in one university for two years. Instead, the programme exposes them to multiple academic and geographical environments.

The programme structure includes study in:

  • Germany
  • Norway
  • Other EMMIR partner locations in Europe, Africa and Asia

The third semester includes a project-based internship and focus module, while the fourth semester allows students to shape their mobility around their Master’s research.

This mobility structure gives students an opportunity to develop a broader understanding of migration and intercultural relations across different social and geographical contexts.

Who Can Apply by Country or Continent?

EMMIR is an international programme involving partner institutions across Europe, Africa and Asia.

The official entry requirements do not establish a race-based restriction and do not state that applicants must belong to a particular country, nationality or continent. The programme is therefore intended for an international applicant pool, subject to meeting the academic, language and other admission requirements.

The programme’s international structure is also reflected in its partner network and student mobility arrangements.

Applicants should nevertheless review the official admission requirements carefully rather than assuming that nationality alone guarantees eligibility.

Programme Costs and Financial Planning

Applicants should distinguish between the different funding categories.

For Erasmus+ scholarship holders, the current programme information states that the scholarship provides €1,400 per month for 24 months, while health insurance, registration and student service fees are covered.

For non-fee-paying self-funded students, participation costs are waived and health insurance, registration and student service fees are covered, but students must finance their living and mobility expenses.

For fee-paying students, the current participation cost is €4,500 per semester, in addition to living and travel expenses.

Applicants should therefore select their funding route carefully when completing the application.

Click HERE to view programme Cost and Funding opportunities

Programme Start Date

EMMIR Edition 14 is scheduled to begin on:

1 September 2027

The programme begins with orientation and an intensive phase before the first semester officially proceeds.

Students admitted to the programme are expected to participate in the programme in person. EMMIR’s current application procedures state that the programme is not offered as a fully online degree and that students are expected to arrive in Oldenburg for the beginning of the programme.

Important Dates for EMMIR Edition 14

Event Date
Applications open 1 October 2026
Scholarship application deadline 20 December 2026
Non-fee-paying application deadline 20 December 2026
Application submission time 23:59 CET
Fee-paying application deadline Until places are assigned, latest 15 July 2027
Admission notifications Beginning/mid-April 2027
Orientation 1 September 2027
Programme start September 2027
Semester 1 October–December 2027
Semester 2 January–May/June 2028
Project-based internship June/July–November 2028
Thesis period December 2028–June 2029
Thesis submission 30 June 2029
Graduation September 2029

The dates above reflect the current EMMIR Edition 14 programme timeline.

Important Advice for Applicants

Because EMMIR is a competitive international Master’s programme, prospective applicants should begin preparing their applications well before the deadline.

Applicants should:

  1. Confirm that their academic background is relevant to migration and intercultural relations.
  2. Check that their first degree meets the required grade level.
  3. Gather their academic transcripts and certificates.
  4. Prepare evidence of relevant knowledge in migration studies, intercultural relations and empirical methods.
  5. Prepare their CV.
  6. Write a strong Statement of Purpose explaining their motivation.
  7. Prepare evidence of English-language proficiency where required.
  8. Check whether they qualify for an English-language waiver.
  9. Determine whether they are applying for an Erasmus+ scholarship, a non-fee-paying place or a fee-paying place.
  10. Register on eMundus and complete the application carefully.
  11. Ensure that all uploaded documents are in English or accompanied by official translations where necessary.
  12. Submit the complete application before the relevant deadline.

Beware of Unofficial EMMIR Groups

Applicants should also be careful about unofficial communication channels.

EMMIR states that its team does not operate official WhatsApp, Telegram, Facebook or other privately created groups for applicants.

Official questions concerning applications should be directed to the EMMIR team through its official communication channels. The programme also advises applicants to submit questions early and allow up to two weeks for responses during busy periods around application deadlines.

This is particularly important during the application period, when applicants may encounter unofficial social media pages, groups or individuals claiming to represent the programme.

Why EMMIR Is a Distinctive Master’s Opportunity

EMMIR offers more than a conventional Master’s programme in which students remain at one university throughout their degree.

Its structure combines:

  • Migration studies
  • Intercultural relations
  • International mobility
  • Multidisciplinary academic training
  • Research
  • Professional development
  • Project-based internship experience
  • Master’s thesis research
  • Exposure to European, African and Asian academic contexts

The programme’s four-semester structure is specifically designed around mobility and interdisciplinary learning, allowing students to develop both academic expertise and practical competencies relevant to migration-related professional environments.

Conclusion

The European Master in Migration and Intercultural Relations (EMMIR) Edition 14 (2027–2029) is a major international Master’s opportunity for graduates interested in migration, intercultural relations, social sciences and related fields.

The two-year Erasmus Mundus programme combines academic study with international mobility, research and practical experience. Students begin their studies in Germany, continue in Norway, undertake an individual mobility and internship component, and complete their Master’s thesis during the final semester.

For applicants seeking financial support, the programme offers a limited number of Erasmus+ scholarships. Current EMMIR information states that scholarship holders receive €1,400 per month for 24 months, alongside coverage of health insurance, university registration and student service fees.

The most important deadline for applicants seeking an Erasmus+ scholarship or a non-fee-paying study place is 20 December 2026 at 23:59 CET. Fee-paying applicants may apply later, subject to availability, with the latest possible deadline currently listed as 15 July 2027.

Prospective applicants should begin preparing early, carefully review the entry requirements, assemble their academic and language documentation, develop a strong Statement of Purpose, and ensure that their application is complete before the applicable deadline.

For applicants passionate about understanding migration and intercultural relations from an international, interdisciplinary and practical perspective, EMMIR provides an opportunity to pursue a Master’s degree across multiple academic and geographical environments while becoming part of an international network focused on one of the most important issues shaping contemporary societies.

item.content:encoded:
The European Court of Auditors (ECA) offers traineeships for university students, graduates and, in specific programmes, doctoral students who want to gain practical experience working within a European Union institution. These traineeships provide an opportunity to contribute to work relating to EU finances, policies, administration, communications, law, technology and other areas while developing professional skills in an international public-sector environment.

The ECA currently offers traineeship opportunities across areas including audit, translation, communications, institutional relations, legal services, general administration, library management, information technology and artificial intelligence. Successful trainees work alongside experienced professionals and are assigned a supervisor who supports their integration into the team and monitors their workload.

For the March 2027 traineeship session, applications open on 1 October 2026, with the application deadline set for 30 November 2026 at midnight Luxembourg time.

About the European Court of Auditors

The European Court of Auditors is the European Union’s external auditor. Its work contributes to accountability and transparency in the management of EU finances.

For trainees, this creates an opportunity to gain first-hand experience of how an EU institution operates and how professional teams contribute to areas that affect European policies, programmes and public resources.

The ECA explains that its traineeships are designed to help European students and graduates gain their first experience of working in EU public administration. Trainees work on meaningful assignments while developing practical knowledge and professional networks.

What Do ECA Trainees Do?

The nature of the work depends on the department and traineeship programme.

Audit traineeships

Trainees working in audit may support professional auditors as they:

  • Analyse the impact of EU policies.
  • Examine how EU programmes and resources are implemented.
  • Identify areas where improvements may be needed.
  • Check for possible financial irregularities.
  • Contribute to audit-related assignments and research.
  • Potentially travel with an audit team to another EU country for fieldwork.

This gives trainees the opportunity to observe how EU auditors carry out their work beyond the institutional setting and gain practical exposure to public-sector auditing.

Non-audit traineeships

Trainees in non-audit departments join ongoing projects and work with project teams under the supervision of a project manager or experienced team member.

Possible areas include:

  • Translation
  • Communications
  • Institutional relations
  • Legal services
  • General administration
  • Library management
  • Information technology
  • Artificial intelligence

The precise work will depend on the available traineeship and the department in which the successful applicant is placed.

European Court of Auditors Traineeship Programmes

The ECA provides several different traineeship pathways. Eligibility requirements and monthly allowances vary depending on the programme.

1. Standard ECA Traineeships

The standard traineeship programme is intended for university students and graduates whose fields of study are relevant to the work of the European Court of Auditors.

Successful candidates normally undertake a six-month traineeship in Luxembourg, although the ECA notes that the duration may be shorter in exceptional circumstances.

The standard traineeship sessions cover:

  • 1 April to 30 September, or
  • 1 October to 31 March of the following year.

The allowance for the standard traineeship is €2,000 per month. The ECA may offer unpaid traineeships in cases where the trainee already receives an allowance from another organisation.

2. Artificial Intelligence Traineeships

The ECA also offers specialised traineeships in artificial intelligence and related technology fields.

These opportunities are designed for recent university graduates and doctoral students with academic backgrounds such as:

  • Artificial intelligence
  • Computer science
  • Data science
  • Information technology
  • Similar disciplines relevant to AI projects

AI trainees receive an allowance of €2,500 per month. Where a trainee already receives an allowance from another organisation, such as a university, the ECA may provide only the difference up to the €2,500 monthly limit.

The AI traineeship therefore provides an opportunity for qualified candidates to gain practical experience working on AI-related projects within an EU institution.

3. Positive Action Programme for Trainees with a Disability

The ECA also operates a Positive Action Programme for trainees with a disability. The programme provides an additional route for people with recognised long-term physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairments.

The ECA offers two traineeship positions per year under this programme for EU nationals with a recognised disability.

Successful trainees receive an allowance of €2,300 per month.

The programme also provides for reasonable accommodation, meaning that the ECA may adapt equipment or working practices where necessary to enable trainees with disabilities to participate on an equal basis, provided that the requested measures do not impose an undue burden on its services.

Applicants under this programme must provide evidence of their recognised disability. Acceptable evidence may include an official document from a national authority or accredited body, or a recent medical certificate meeting the ECA’s requirements.

4. Traineeships for Supreme Audit Institutions in EU Candidate Countries

A separate programme is available for auditors working for the Supreme Audit Institutions (SAIs) of countries that are candidates for EU accession.

These traineeships are intended to provide practical experience of European integration and the day-to-day operation of an EU institution. The experience is intended to support participating SAIs in their preparations for EU accession.

The allowance for this programme is €2,000 per month.

Applicants must:

  • Be actively employed by the SAI of an EU candidate country.
  • Be a national of that candidate country.
  • Have an interest in practical training related to one of the ECA’s areas of activity.
  • Have good knowledge of at least one of the ECA’s working languages, English or French.
  • Have never previously undertaken a traineeship at the ECA.

Unlike the standard application route, selection for SAI traineeships is organised directly by the relevant Supreme Audit Institution, which proposes candidates to the ECA. Successful candidates then receive a traineeship offer following an interview with the ECA.

Standard Traineeship Eligibility Requirements

For the standard ECA traineeship programme, applicants must satisfy specific eligibility conditions.

According to the ECA’s current information, applicants must:

  1. Be a national of an EU Member State.
  2. Have completed at least four semesters of university study in a field relevant to the ECA’s work.
  3. Have a very good knowledge of one official EU language and a satisfactory knowledge of a second official EU language.
  4. Not have previously worked for an EU institution, body or agency in any capacity, including as a trainee.

The ECA’s rules also establish eligibility conditions concerning previous employment or traineeship experience within EU institutions and the applicant’s educational background. Applicants should therefore carefully review the official rules before submitting an application.

Eligibility for the AI Traineeship

The AI traineeship has more specialised requirements.

Applicants must:

  • Be nationals of an EU Member State.
  • Have completed university studies equivalent to a diploma of at least three years, or currently be undertaking doctoral studies.
  • Have studied AI, computer science, data science, information technology or a similar discipline relevant to the ECA’s AI projects.
  • Have very good knowledge of one official EU language and satisfactory knowledge of a second.
  • Have a sound level of English, with at least C1 level in understanding, speaking and writing.
  • Not have previously worked for an EU institution, body or agency in any capacity, including as a trainee.

For the AI traineeship, applicants are required to provide a CV in Europass format, a cover letter and a recommendation letter as part of the selection process.

Eligibility for the Positive Action Programme

Applicants for the Positive Action Programme must:

  • Be nationals of an EU Member State.
  • Have completed at least four semesters of university study in a field relevant to the ECA’s work.
  • Have very good knowledge of one official EU language and satisfactory knowledge of a second.
  • Not have worked for an EU institution, body or agency in any capacity, including as a trainee.
  • Have a recognised disability.

Applicants must also provide appropriate documentation confirming their disability.

Areas of Study and Professional Interest

The ECA accepts applications across a broad range of fields connected to its institutional work.

The areas specifically identified by the ECA include:

  • Auditing
  • Public administration
  • Economics
  • Finance
  • Law
  • Communications
  • Translation
  • Institutional relations
  • General administration
  • Library management
  • Information technology
  • Artificial intelligence
  • Computer science
  • Data science
  • Related technology disciplines

The exact academic background required depends on the particular traineeship programme and available placement.

Candidates should therefore assess the requirements of the specific traineeship before applying rather than assuming that every academic discipline qualifies.

Learn More HERE

Financial Support and Monthly Allowance

One of the important features of the ECA traineeships is that several of the programmes provide a monthly financial allowance.

The current allowances are:

Traineeship Programme Monthly Allowance
Standard traineeship €2,000
AI traineeship €2,500
Positive Action Programme €2,300
SAI traineeship €2,000

The ECA notes that allowance arrangements can differ between programmes. For example, an AI trainee who already receives an allowance from another organisation may receive only the difference up to the €2,500 ECA allowance ceiling. Standard traineeships may also be unpaid where the trainee already receives an allowance from another organisation.

Applicants should therefore check the rules applicable to the specific programme for which they are applying.

Professional Experience and Learning Opportunities

The value of the ECA traineeship extends beyond the monthly allowance.

Trainees become part of a professional working environment and gain practical experience within an EU institution. They work under supervision and contribute to actual projects and activities.

Depending on their department, trainees may gain experience in:

  • EU public administration
  • Financial and performance auditing
  • Policy analysis
  • Institutional relations
  • Communications
  • Legal work
  • Public-sector administration
  • Information technology
  • Artificial intelligence
  • Research and analytical work
  • Project management

The ECA also emphasises the importance of learning through interaction with fellow trainees. Trainees begin their placements as a cohort, allowing them to develop professional relationships and build networks that can continue beyond the traineeship.

Working with Experienced Professionals

Each trainee is assigned a traineeship supervisor who helps the trainee integrate into the team and monitors their workload.

This structure is particularly useful for students and recent graduates who may be entering a professional institutional environment for the first time.

Rather than simply observing the work of the ECA, trainees are expected to contribute to ongoing projects and activities under appropriate supervision.

Location of the Traineeship

The main location for the ECA traineeships is Luxembourg, where successful standard trainees spend their placement working within the European Court of Auditors.

For standard traineeships, the ECA describes the placement as an opportunity to spend six months in Luxembourg contributing to the work of the institution.

For audit trainees, there may also be opportunities to travel with audit teams to other EU Member States when fieldwork requires it.

March 2027 ECA Traineeship Session

The European Court of Auditors operates two regular traineeship sessions each year.

For the upcoming session relevant to this application cycle, the schedule is:

  • Applications open: 1 October 2026
  • Application deadline: 30 November 2026
  • Deadline time: Midnight, Luxembourg time
  • Traineeship session: March/April 2027 cycle, according to the applicable programme schedule

The ECA’s application table identifies the March 2027 session as opening on Thursday, 1 October 2026 and closing on Monday, 30 November 2026 at midnight Luxembourg time.

Applicants should submit their applications before the deadline because applications are accepted through the ECA’s designated online application process.

How to Apply

Applicants for standard traineeships and the Positive Action Programme must apply through the Official ECA Application Form.

The ECA specifically states that applicants must click the application option associated with the open traineeship session. Applications cannot be submitted through alternative methods.

For the AI traineeships, applicants should follow the specific instructions published by the ECA for the relevant AI call.

For SAI traineeships, applicants should contact the relevant department of the Supreme Audit Institution where they work because the selection process is organised directly through those institutions.

APPLY HERE

Documents for the Application

Depending on the programme, applicants may be required to provide supporting documents.

For the AI traineeship, the ECA specifically identifies:

  • A CV in Europass format
  • A cover letter
  • A recommendation letter

Other traineeship programmes may have additional requirements through their respective application forms.

Applicants should carefully read the requirements of their chosen programme and make sure that all requested information and supporting documents are supplied before submitting the application.

Important Consideration for Non-EU Applicants

The standard ECA traineeship programme is not an open worldwide traineeship.

The current ECA eligibility requirements specify EU Member State nationality for standard traineeships, AI traineeships and the Positive Action Programme.

This means that applicants from countries outside the European Union should not assume that they are eligible for the standard ECA traineeship simply because they are international students or graduates.

There is, however, a separate SAI traineeship route for auditors from countries that are candidates for EU accession. That programme has its own eligibility and nomination procedure.

Why Consider an ECA Traineeship?

An ECA traineeship can provide an important early-career opportunity for eligible students and graduates interested in European institutions, public administration, auditing, finance, law, communications, technology and related areas.

The experience can help participants:

  • Gain practical experience within an EU institution.
  • Understand how European public administration operates.
  • Work with experienced professionals.
  • Develop technical and professional skills.
  • Contribute to real institutional projects.
  • Build an international professional network.
  • Gain exposure to EU policies and financial management.
  • Explore potential career interests in public-sector and international organisations.
  • Develop experience relevant to future academic or professional opportunities.

The cohort structure also gives trainees the opportunity to build relationships with other young professionals participating in the programme.

Key Details at a Glance

Opportunity: European Court of Auditors Traineeships

Institution: European Court of Auditors

Opportunity type: Paid traineeship

Location: Luxembourg

Main fields: Audit, finance, public administration, law, communications, translation, institutional relations, administration, library management, IT, artificial intelligence, computer science, data science and related areas.

Standard allowance: €2,000 per month

AI traineeship allowance: €2,500 per month

Positive Action Programme allowance: €2,300 per month

SAI traineeship allowance: €2,000 per month

Standard eligibility: Primarily EU nationals who have completed at least four semesters of relevant university study and meet the language and previous EU employment/traineeship requirements.

AI eligibility: EU nationals who are recent graduates or doctoral students in relevant AI and technology disciplines and meet the language requirements.

Application opening: 1 October 2026

Application deadline: 30 November 2026 at midnight Luxembourg time

Application method: Official ECA online application process for standard and Positive Action traineeships.

Visit HERE to learn more about the European Court of Auditors Traineeships 2027.

Conclusion

The European Court of Auditors Traineeships 2027 provide eligible students, graduates and specialised applicants with an opportunity to gain practical experience inside a major European Union institution. Depending on the programme, participants can work in areas ranging from auditing and public administration to communications, law, information technology and artificial intelligence.

The programme is particularly relevant for candidates interested in EU institutions, public finance, auditing, governance, international administration, law, communications and emerging technologies. With monthly allowances of up to €2,500 for AI traineeships and the opportunity to work alongside experienced professionals in Luxembourg, the traineeship can provide substantial practical and professional exposure.

For applicants interested in the March 2027 session, the important date to remember is 30 November 2026 at midnight Luxembourg time. Candidates should review the specific eligibility requirements for their chosen traineeship, prepare their supporting documents carefully and submit their applications through the official ECA application system before the deadline.

Official information and application details are available through the European Court of Auditors’ traineeship page.
